Hi, how are you today?
I'm doing fine. My problem is that my boss keeps hitting on a co-worker, who really doesn't like the guy. What can I do to make it stop?
Boy, that's a tough one. You've got to handle a problem like that pretty diplomatically. Have you talked to your co-worker, the one the boss hits on?

I've tried to bring it up with her indirectly, but it's an uncomfortable issue, you know? She is really upset, and I don't know whether it's my place to handle this kind of thing. It's more of an HR issue, but should I go to HR? Will that help, or just get me in trouble? I don't know.
That's a good question, and I don't know the answer. It depends on your HR department. Have you suggested that the co-worker talk to HR? Is there an anonymous system for filing complaints?

No, the company hasn't set up a system for passing along info that way. I don't know if she has talked to HR. She might not have because she's worried that it'll get back to her boss, and she'll get punished. I'd like to be supportive, even if I can't help solve the problem.
That's a good attitude. You want to be supportive and helpful. You sound like a good co-worker. Remember that the problem did not start with you, so you do not need to feel responsible for it.

Thanks for your words of encouragement? Maybe there is little I can do, but I don't want to let the problem fester. She's a great co-worker and a great worker. We need her on the team. What do you think a good first step would be?

That's a good question. I would show support for her and empathize with her and her situation. Do you have lunch with her? Can you send her a text letting her know she's valued? She might appreciate that.
Sometimes we have lunch, but usually she just eats at her desk. I could easily send her texts of encouragement.
Ok. That's a good first step. I think you have a way forward with this. Maybe after a few texts, you can sit down and talk about solutions in detail, like going to HR.
Ok. I'll try sending a couple of texts every day. Then I'll see if she wants to have lunch outside with me when the weather gets better.
That's a good positive step. I think that you've got a pretty handle on the situation. Good for you!
Thanks. The boss is pretty good at his job. He know how to manage projects and he's good with clients. There is just this one thing that he gets wrong and somebody needs to get him to stop.
I understand that you're frustrated and sad. I would feel the same way too. I think that anyone else in your situation would feel the same way.

Thanks. I guess I just have to accept things as they are. I can't afford to leave this job, and it's impossible to find another job at this time. Plus I don't want to abandon my co-worker in her time of need.
Well, you have to do what is right for yourself. If you find a better job, think seriously about taking it. Your co-worker will not be there forever. You have a responsibility to yourself.
True. I hadn't thought of it that way. I should consider my needs. Thanks!
You're welcome! I'm glad that I was able to help you!
I feel a lot better now. I start sending text messages to my co-worker on Monday. Thanks! Have a good day!
You too! Have a great day, and good luck with work!
Good evening
Hello. How are you?
ok. How can I be of service tonight
I'm just feeling sad and depressed over the breakup that I described above. Hoping for some inspiration.
Tell me more please I am all ears
I feel so betrayed. I was completely caught off guard. Now I don't know what to do with myself.
When did this happen, How long ago
Just this last week. I came home from work early Thursday. I guess I should have texted first so he could get rid of the guy. Or maybe not. Maybe it's better that I found out.
So you had been together for awhile and all of  a sudden he has another person in his life
We were together almost ten years. Over nine and a half. I had no idea. I don't think the guy is even someone he really cares about. I don't know.
Was this guy an associate of yours as well
So basically this guy was a stranger that you know of.
Yes that's right, I'd never seen him before.
Did you have any children between you
No, it was just the two of us. And two cats. Who are still here with me. There's that at least.
DiId your partner work also
Just from home. Self-published author, some online work, stuff like that. He made about as much as I did, I wasn't the sole breadwinner or anything.
Maybe the time on his hands enabled to him meet someone while you were working. Did he have a following that you knew of
has there been habits like this before

Maybe it did. There are some fans of his work on social media, and he's on all the popular social media sights. I don't know if he me the guy online or what. There hasn't been anything like this before that I know of. Maybe there was. I trusted him and didn't look at his messages or anything.
His actions none the less are not right
Do you have an idea his websites
No, they weren't, I agree there. He took all his devices with him. I can see his stuff from a user point of view, like anyone else in the public could, but nothing of his personal stuff.
The fact that he cheated on you and I assume you broke up with him is hard
He must have a special account that people can access to, can you possibly find it out
Yeah, we're over. And it is hard. I'll get past it I suppose. I don't think I could, but I don't really want to anyway at this point. It's not going to help us get back together or anything.
Maybe you need to focus on you now, and plan your days ahead.
I think you're right. Just look forward.
Had you known before hand it might be of help, but the sudden impact does not make it any better
if you look back you will have regrets. If you look forward you will see a future
You're right. Thank you for listening. I feel a little better already. I'll get through this. Me and the cats :-)
Take a cup of coffee, sit and write your thoughts then burn them
Sounds like a good plan.
Write your past down then throw it into a fire
Thank you again. I'm going to go ahead and wrap up the conversation. I'll be okay.
OK. Have a blessed night.
You too. Take care.
Hello! How are you doing today?
I'm good thanks but pretty frustrated too be honest. It's my friend who has taken to being a pain on Facebook
I'm sorry to hear you are frustrated! I'm gonna do my best to understand and talk through your issue. :) Your friend is being a pain on face book in what way?
He's all of a sudden got an opinion on everything and tries to pull me into arguments with other friends.
It sounds like he didn't use to blast his opinion in the past or include you in arguments, is that true?

That is true yes. It's like the world has to listen to his opinion and only his matters and he won't listen to reason. It's very frustrating and it makes me not want to talk to him. My eyes literally roll when I see a post from him.

Oh I see! I get where you are coming from. I have a few friends that no matter how long you discuss, they won't let the conversation end unless "they are right." It seems like your friend doesn't like it when he is wrong?
Absolutely and I'm not sure how to broach this with him. I actually feel like it is damaging his reputation. Other friends of ours feel the same way. Not sure what to do?

Gotcha so not only are you frustrated with what he is doing, but you are also worried about his reputation! First of all, can I ask if he is just your friend online or if you hangout with him in person too?
That's correct. He is actually a close friend and I wonder what has changed recently to make him like this. I've known him for over 20 years.

Okay I see. From personal experience, the best way to confront someone who likes to do most of their confrontations online, is in person. Since he is so used to almost "hiding" behind a screen, his feelings will be more vulnerable and real if you discuss your concerns in person.
Actually I've never thought of it like that. Perhaps a couple of us can have a conversation with him in person. Honestly some off his views are disgusting. I think this needs to stop.

A suggestion I would make would be to hangout with him in person, and bring up the issues that you and your friends have been seeing. But it's important to not make him feel overwhelmed. Almost like he is being "ganged up on."
Yes that's good advice, I think we need to be tactful and raise it in the right way. Have you ever experienced something like this with a friend yourself?

I can tell that you care about this person as a friend, but you are worried that the way he thinks and talks may ruin that in a way. Make sure to let him know these concerns! It will show him that you guys truly are doing it out of love.
And yes I have actually had a very similar experience! Let me explain
Ok sure please do

One of my best friend's and roommate, had a very hard time separating friendship and roommate issues. It caused a lot of issues in the relationships with our friends. She had a tendency to discuss issues over text and didn't like doing it in person. But we realized, the problem with that is that you can't tell the emotion behind messages on a screen. But once we talked in person, our issues were solved because we could hear the intended emotions behind what we were saying

Yeah that's useful. I think you are right in that the ambiguity of social interaction online makes him more inclined to say extreme thinks, perhaps to get a reaction. The more I think about it, perhaps this could be an indication that there is something he is dealing with and may be lashing out.

Yes exactly. It sounds like he might have other reasonings behind his actions. And you guys talking to him as friends in person, would show him that you care and that he is in a safe environment. He doesn't need to be so extreme
Yeah I think that's definitely the way forward. Listen this has really helped so thanks for the suggestions and sharing your own experiences.
Yes of course! I wish you the best in overcoming this hard time with your friend. I believe that you guys will be able to talk through it since it's a newer issue. :)
I hope so too. Nice to talk to you and thanks again.
Of course! Have a good rest of your day
Thanks
Hey, I hope you don't mind me reaching out.
Not at all, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I had a bit of a breakdown at work recently. It was just... a lot.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what happened?
Yeah, I just couldn't hold it together anymore. There's been this constant harassment, but I haven’t addressed it.
That sounds incredibly tough and unfair. Thank you for trusting me with this. How long has this been going on?
It's been months, maybe longer. I think I ignored it at first because I thought it would stop.
I can understand hoping it would go away. It’s not easy to confront such issues. How does it make you feel to talk about it now?
Honestly, it's a mix of relief and fear. Relief to finally say it out loud, but fear of what comes next.
Those feelings make a lot of sense. It can be scary to think about the next steps, but voicing it is a strong first step.
Yeah, I guess I was worried people would think I'm overreacting.
Your feelings are completely valid. Workplace harassment is serious, and it’s important to take it seriously.
Thank you. I keep replaying moments in my head, wondering if I should have done something different.
It's natural to question past actions, but it’s important to be kind to yourself. You're doing the best you can.
I really appreciate that. I guess I need to figure out my next steps.
Absolutely. Have you thought about what feels right for you moving forward? Maybe speaking to HR or a trusted colleague?
I’ve thought about going to HR, but I’m scared about the repercussions.
That’s understandable, and your concerns are valid. Is there someone at work you trust who could support you with this?
There might be a couple of people, but I'm not sure if they'd want to get involved.
Perhaps starting a conversation with them could help gauge their willingness to support you. It could be comforting not to face this alone.
That’s a good idea. I’ll think about who I can talk to. It helps to know that it’s not hopeless.
It's definitely not hopeless. You have options and I'm here to help you explore them. You’re not alone in this.
Thank you so much. I feel a bit lighter after talking it through.
I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, I'm just a message away if you need to talk again.
Thanks, I really appreciate it.
Hey there, thanks for being here today.
Hi Sarah! I'm here to listen. How have you been doing lately?
It's been tough. I started therapy recently, and it's brought up a lot of emotions.
Starting therapy can be a big step. It’s completely normal for it to stir up feelings. Do you want to share what's been coming up for you?
Yeah, I guess. The breakup and everything at work...it just feels like too much sometimes.
It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed with everything you've been through.
I agreed to therapy thinking it would help, but facing everything head-on is scarier than I thought.
I can imagine how that might feel daunting. But it’s also courageous. It's the beginning of healing, even if it feels hard right now.
I keep thinking about the harassment at work. Ignoring it for so long just made me feel so powerless.
That must be incredibly difficult to deal with. It’s not easy to confront such issues, especially in a work environment.
And the whole thing with my ex didn't help. I felt so betrayed and just... lost.
It’s heartbreaking to go through betrayal like that. Your feelings are completely valid, and it's okay to feel lost.
Thank you. I feel like I'm just venting but it's nice to have someone listen.
I'm here to listen anytime you need. You're going through a lot, and it's important to let those feelings out.
I’ve also been worried about my co-worker. The way our boss behaved with her... she seems uneasy, and I wish I could do more.
It speaks volumes about your compassion that you’re concerned for her, too. Have you had a chance to talk with her about it?
Not really. I don't want to overstep, but I also want her to know she's not alone.
That's really thoughtful. Maybe just letting her know you're there if she needs someone to talk to could mean a lot.
I'll try that. It's reassuring to hear I’m not overreacting.
You're not overreacting at all. These are significant issues, and your feelings about them matter.
I have to keep reminding myself that it's okay to speak up, even if it's hard.
Absolutely. Your voice is important. And it’s okay to take small steps. You’re doing a lot just by starting to talk about it.
Thanks for reminding me. I don't feel so alone knowing I have support.
You’re never alone in this. Whenever you need to share or need reassurance, I’m here.
Hey, can I talk to you about something that's been on my mind?
Of course, Sarah. What's been happening?
I found out recently that my close friend has been dealing with depression, and it's really worrying me.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must be difficult to know someone you care about is struggling. How are you handling it?
Honestly, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed. I want to help but I'm not sure how.
Wanting to support your friend shows how much you care. It's okay not to have all the answers. Have you been able to talk to them about it?
We talked a little. They admitted things have been tough but didn’t go into much detail. I don’t want to push them.
It's great that they opened up to you a bit. Listening can be very supportive too. Have you been able to share some of what you're feeling with your therapist?
Yeah, I mentioned it in therapy, but I feel guilty for focusing on my own feelings when my friend is the one struggling.
Your feelings are valid too, Sarah. It’s natural to feel for your friend, but taking care of yourself is important. It helps you to be there for them.
That makes sense. I guess I'm just scared of making things worse, you know?
That’s a common fear, but being there for your friend and offering a listening ear can do a lot of good. Have you noticed any changes in how you both interact since you found out?
I’m trying to be more present when we're together. I feel like they've become more withdrawn, and it hurts to see.
It's tough seeing someone you care about in pain. But showing up and letting them know they're not alone is supportive.
I’ll keep that in mind. I just wish there was more I could do.
Your friend is lucky to have someone as caring as you. When you're ready, maybe suggesting they talk to a professional could help.
That’s a good point. Maybe I'll bring it up gently if the time feels right. It just feels like there’s so much to balance between work, therapy, and now worrying about my friend.
It's a lot to juggle, for sure. Remember, you're not alone in this. How has work been since you started therapy?
It's gotten better, slowly. I’m trying to set boundaries and leave work at the office.
That sounds like progress. It's so important to set boundaries for your well-being. Do you feel therapy has helped you in that regard?
Definitely. Having someone to talk to about these things has been grounding. I just need to remind myself to practice what I'm learning.
It's wonderful to hear therapy is helping. Implementing what you’ve learned can take time, so be patient with yourself.
Thanks. I’ll try to be kinder to myself. I really appreciate you listening and offering advice.
Anytime, Sarah. Remember, you're doing your best, and that counts for a lot. Don't hesitate to reach out again if you need to talk.
Thanks again. I’ll definitely reach out. Take care.
You too, take care.
Hey, I hope you're available to chat for a bit. I could use some support right now.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been going on?
Well, I finally told my colleague that I have feelings for him, and we decided to start dating.
That's a big step! How are you feeling about it?
I'm feeling a mix of excitement and worry. It's great to be with someone I connect with, but I'm also scared about how things might change at work.
It's understandable to have those mixed feelings. Entering a new relationship is exciting but can also bring changes. What's your biggest concern right now?
I guess I'm worried about how our colleagues might react. We both agreed to keep things professional, but gossip can be brutal.
Office dynamics can be tricky. It sounds like you two have a good plan in place to stay professional. Do you think there's someone in the office you can confide in if things get challenging?
I do have a couple of colleagues who I trust. It's just that my last breakdown at work left me feeling a bit vulnerable. I'm trying to avoid that happening again.
It's great you have people you trust. And remember, you’ve come a long way since that incident. How have you been managing stress since starting therapy?
Therapy has been really helpful. It's taught me ways to set boundaries and be more open about my feelings. I think it’s why I felt ready to approach my colleague.
That's wonderful to hear. Taking those steps for personal growth can really make a difference. Have you talked to your therapist about starting this new relationship?
Not yet, but I'm planning on bringing it up in my next session. My therapist has really helped me gain perspective on my relationships.
That sounds like a great idea. Having professional guidance can really clarify things. How are things on the friendship front with your close friend?
My friend is still struggling, which has been hard to watch. I've been trying to be there for them without overstepping.
It must be tough to see someone you care about go through a hard time. How are you handling being supportive without taking on too much yourself?
I try to listen and offer support when I can but also remind myself that their journey is separate from mine, and I need to set limits for my own well-being.
That's a healthy approach. Remember, you can only do so much, and caring for yourself is crucial. How do you unwind after emotionally exhausting days?
I've been getting into yoga and reading a lot lately. It helps me center myself and escape my thoughts for a while.
Those sound like amazing outlets. Staying grounded and finding time for yourself can be so rejuvenating. Is there anything else on your mind that you'd like to share?
No, I think that's it for now. Thanks for listening. It really helps to talk things through.
Anytime, Sarah. I'm here whenever you need to chat. Take care of yourself, okay?
I will. Thanks again!
Hey, do you have a moment to talk?
Of course, Sarah. What's going on?
I had an argument with Jack today, you know, the colleague I'm dating.

Those are huge decisions, and it's natural to feel apprehensive. It's important that you feel ready. Have you been able to discuss these fears with Jack?
Not really, the conversation usually turns into a debate instead of a discussion. It's like we're on different pages sometimes.
I can understand how frustrating that must be. Communication is key, but it's also hard to stay calm during intense discussions. Do you think setting aside time to talk would help?
I think it might. I'm just worried that my fears will be dismissed again, and I don't want to feel that way anymore.
It's important that both of you feel heard. Maybe framing it as a series of conversations rather than a one-time talk might help ease the pressure.
That's a good point. Maybe if we take it slow, I won't feel as anxious. I just hate feeling like I'm holding things up.
You’re not holding anything up by wanting to make thoughtful decisions. It's important to move at a pace that feels right for you. Have you reached out to your therapist about these feelings?
Yeah, I'm seeing them tomorrow. They've been helpful, especially since I started painting.
That's great to hear. Painting sounds like a wonderful outlet for you. Have you found it helps with processing these emotions?
It really does. It's like a form of meditation for me. It gives me the space to think things through away from all the noise.
It’s wonderful you have an outlet like that. It’s important to have those moments of reflection. Is there anything else that's been weighing on you recently?
I guess I'm still feeling pressure from work. Even though I'm working fewer hours, the expectations feel as high as ever.
That sounds really challenging. It's hard when expectations don't align with capacity. Have you been able to communicate your boundaries to your boss?
I have, but it's almost like they nod, agree, and then nothing changes. I'm worried about my performance reviews.

It must be frustrating to feel unheard at work. Staying true to your boundaries is really important. Do you think there’s a way to document these discussions with your boss so there’s a record of your concerns?
That's a good idea. I think having it written down might help. At least it would make me feel like actions are being taken.
It's always worth a try, and it might give you some peace of mind knowing there's a trail. Remember, taking care of your mental health is just as important as your career, if not more.
Thank you for saying that. I tend to forget sometimes. This whole conversation has made me feel lighter.
I'm really glad to hear that, Sarah. Remember, you’re doing a fantastic job navigating all these challenges. You’re stronger than you give yourself credit for.
Thank you for being here and listening. It means a lot to know I have someone to talk to.
Anytime, Sarah. I'm here whenever you need to talk. Take care of yourself.
Hey, thanks for being here. I could really use someone to listen right now.
Of course, Sarah. I'm here for you. What's been on your mind?
It's been a lot lately. My therapist suggested mindfulness exercises to help with my anxiety.
Mindfulness can be really helpful. How are you finding it so far?
Honestly, I haven't started yet. I feel kind of overwhelmed by everything else.
That's understandable. Sometimes starting something new can add to the stress. What's been overwhelming you the most?
Well, there was that argument with Jack about our future plans. It left me feeling really unsettled.
It's tough when future plans aren't aligning. Do you want to share more about the argument?
We were talking about moving in together and it kind of spiraled from there. I guess I'm scared of losing my independence.
It's natural to feel that way. Balancing a relationship and personal space can be challenging. Have you been able to discuss these concerns with him since the argument?
Not really. It feels like we both need some space to process things first.
Taking time to process can be wise. Maybe mindfulness could help you sort through these emotions too?
I suppose it could, but I'm also distracted by work stress. My boss's feedback hasn't been as encouraging as I hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that. It can be discouraging when hard work isn't recognized. Did the feedback touch on anything specific?
It was more general, but it left me feeling inadequate, like I'm not meeting expectations.
Feeling inadequate can be really tough, especially when you're already dealing with so much. Remember, you've handled difficult situations before.
That's true. I've come this far, and I guess a part of me knows I can handle this too. But I can't help but feel stuck sometimes.
Feeling stuck is a common experience, especially with so many pressures. Maybe pinpointing small steps could help ease that feeling?
Small steps could work. My therapist did mention focusing on manageable goals, like starting with one mindfulness session a day.
That sounds like a great first step. Even small progress can bring a sense of accomplishment and relief.
Thanks for reminding me of that. I want to believe it'll get better. Perhaps I'll try a mindfulness session tonight.
That's a positive move. Remember, I'm here anytime you want to talk or share how it's going.
Thank you. It really helps to have someone to confide in. I appreciate you being here for me.
It's my pleasure. You're doing your best, and that's what matters most. Take care of yourself, Sarah.
Hey, are you around? I could use someone to talk to.
Hi Sarah, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's about Jack... We've decided to take a break.
That sounds tough, especially with everything you've shared about your relationship struggles.
Yeah, it was kind of expected but still hurts.
It's normal to feel that way. Do you want to talk more about what led to the decision?
I think everything just built up over time. The work stress, personal space issues... It all became too much.
That's understandable. It sounds like there were a lot of pressures from different areas.
Yeah, and with his role being part of my work life too, it complicates things further.
Having that overlap can add another layer of stress. How are you coping with this?
Honestly, I'm not sure. I've been trying to immerse myself in painting, as my therapist suggested.
Painting sounds like a great outlet. I'm glad you have something like that to turn to.
It's been helping, but the anxiety is still there, especially after recent arguments.
Have the mindfulness exercises from your therapist been helpful at all?
They help a bit. I just feel overwhelmed sometimes, like I'm juggling too many things.
It sounds like you have a lot on your plate. Remember to be kind to yourself during this time.
I'm trying. It's just hard sometimes, especially with all these changes.
Change can be daunting, but it's also an opportunity for growth. I'm here for you every step of the way.
Thank you, it means a lot. It feels good to have someone to talk to.
You're not alone, Sarah. We'll get through this together.
I know. It's comforting to have a support system.
Absolutely. If you ever feel like you're slipping, whether it's about Jack or anything else, just reach out.
I will. For now, I think I'll focus on painting a bit more this weekend.
That sounds like a perfect plan. Let the creativity flow and take it one day at a time.
Yeah, one step at a time. Thanks again for listening.
Anytime, Sarah. Take care and keep in touch.
Hey, thanks for being here. I just felt like talking.
Of course, Sarah. I'm always here to listen. What's been going on?
Well, I started attending this local art class recently to improve my painting skills.
That's great! I remember how much you enjoyed painting. How is the class going so far?
It’s been nice meeting new people who share the same interest. But, I feel a bit out of place sometimes.
I can understand that. It can be tough to find your footing in a new group. What's making you feel out of place?
I guess it's just that everyone seems so confident and talented. I doubt my own skills compared to them.
It's natural to feel that way in a new environment. Remember, you're there to learn and grow. Everyone starts somewhere.
Yeah, you're right. It's just that old feeling of inadequacy creeping back in, like when I received that feedback at work.
I recall you mentioning that. It sounds like it's been a recurring theme for you. Have you talked to your therapist about these feelings?
I have, actually. They've recommended mindfulness exercises to help manage my anxiety and self-doubt.
That's a good step. Have you been able to incorporate those exercises into your routine?
Trying to, but it's challenging with everything else going on, like the tensions with Jack and work stress.
How are things with Jack lately? Have you both had a chance to talk about the future?
Not really. We decided to take a break after our last argument. It's tough, but I think it might be what we need.
That sounds like a difficult decision. But it takes courage to do what's best for you both. How are you feeling about it?
I'm sad, but also a bit relieved. I guess I need to really focus on myself right now.
Taking time for yourself is important. You've been through a lot and deserve some peace and self-care.
Thanks. I just need to hold onto that thought, especially when things get overwhelming.
You can do this, Sarah. You're taking all the right steps, and your passion for painting is a wonderful outlet.
Thank you. It really helps to hear that. I'll keep trying to find balance.
You're stronger than you think. I'm here whenever you need to talk or just need someone to listen.
I appreciate that more than I can say. I really needed this conversation.
Anytime, Sarah. You're never alone in this.
Hey, I just reconnected with an old college friend. It's been a while since we talked.
That sounds intriguing! How did you two get back in touch?
Actually, he stumbled upon my blog about mental health and reached out. We've been catching up a bit.
That's so nice! Your blog must really resonate with people. How are you feeling about reconnecting?
It's been nice, but it's also brought up a lot of past feelings and memories. I guess I'm a bit overwhelmed.
That makes sense. Old friendships can bring up a lot of emotions. How are you managing those feelings?
I'm trying to keep things in perspective and use what I've learned in therapy. It's just...sometimes it feels like too much.
It's good that you're using your therapeutic tools. Have you talked to your therapist about it?
Not yet. We've been focusing more on my recent breakup and the tension with Jack, my boss-slash-partner.
That sounds like it keeps you pretty occupied. It might help to bring this up with your therapist too when you can.
You're right. I think I just needed to talk it out first. Sometimes, these old connections feel a bit disruptive.
I understand that. It’s okay to feel that way. Maybe there's something positive this old friend can bring to your life again?
True, he was really supportive back in college. It’s nice to have that kind of support again.
Absolutely! It's great that you have someone who can be there for you. How do you see things moving forward with him?
I think we'll just take things slow. I'm not sure how much time I can commit with everything else going on.
Taking it slow sounds like a good plan. It's important to prioritize what feels manageable.
Yeah, I'll try to. I want to focus more on the things that lift me up, like my art classes and my blog.
That sounds like a wonderful focus. Remember to take care of yourself and lean on your support system when needed.
Thanks for listening and for the advice. I really appreciate having this space to talk.
Anytime. I'm here for you whenever you need to chat. Just take it one step at a time.
Hey, I really need to talk about something that happened recently.
Of course, Sarah. What's on your mind?
My parents invited me over for a family gathering last weekend, and it got me thinking a lot.
I remember you mentioned how unexpected visits from them can be overwhelming. How did it go this time?
It was surprisingly calm at first, but as the evening progressed, they started asking about my life choices again.
That sounds challenging. Did their questions make you feel pressured?
Yes, exactly. I felt like they were questioning every decision I’ve made, from cutting back hours at work to my relationship status.
It sounds like they have a lot of opinions about your choices. How did you handle those moments?
I tried to stay calm and explain my perspective, but it just seemed like they weren’t really listening.
That must have been frustrating. What do you wish they understood about your situation?
I just wish they could see that I'm trying to take better care of myself. Reducing work hours and focusing on painting has been really beneficial for my mental health.
You’ve made some significant changes to better support your wellbeing. It's understandable to want their support in these choices.
Exactly. And sometimes I wish they could understand that not everything in life is about career or conventional success.
Absolutely. Success can look different for everyone, and prioritizing mental health is an important form of success.
I guess I just need to find a way to communicate with them that doesn’t lead to tension and anxiety.
It sounds like maintaining an open dialogue is important to you. How do you think you might approach that in future conversations with them?
Maybe I could try setting some boundaries about certain topics, or redirecting the conversation to lighter subjects when it gets too intense.
That sounds like a constructive approach. Setting boundaries can help protect your mental health while still staying connected with them.
Right. I think being prepared with a few key things to say might help me navigate those tough moments.
Having those responses ready might make you feel more in control during those conversations.
I hope so. I just want to feel at ease around them and not dread family gatherings.
It sounds like you really value your relationship with them, even if it can be difficult at times. You're making a lot of thoughtful efforts to improve it.
Thanks, I really am trying. It means a lot to have your support in this.
I'm glad to be here for you. Remember, you're handling a lot and doing it with courage. Don't hesitate to reach out anytime you need to chat.
Hey Sarah, I saw your message about taking a sabbatical from work. How are you feeling about that decision?
Hi! I'm feeling a mix of emotions, to be honest. A bit relieved, but also anxious about stepping away from work.
That makes a lot of sense. It sounds like giving yourself permission to focus on your well-being is a big step.
Yeah, it's just that work has been such a huge part of my identity. I'm worried about how this break might affect my career.
Feeling uncertain about career impacts is understandable. But it seems like prioritizing your mental health could really provide you with more clarity in the long run.
True, I've been stretching myself thin with everything. My therapist suggested the sabbatical might help me regroup and find a balance.
Your therapist seems to have a good point. With everything you've been through, a break could give you time to recharge and focus on what makes you happy.
I hope so. I'm also feeling excited about getting back into writing. The blog has been therapeutic for me.
That's great! Writing can be such a powerful outlet. How does it feel to share your story through your blog?
It's been rewarding but nerve-wracking too. Putting my experiences out there makes me feel vulnerable, but connecting with others going through similar struggles has been eye-opening.
It sounds like you're building a really supportive community. Vulnerability can be challenging, but it often leads to meaningful connections.
Definitely, and that's what I'm trying to keep in mind. I'm also hoping this time off gives me more chances to explore my painting as well.
Exploring new hobbies like painting can be so rejuvenating. How has your art journey been so far?
It's been a lovely escape. Losing myself in colors and creativity helps calm my mind. Plus, attending the local art class has been a wonderful way to meet people.
That sounds amazing, Sarah. It must feel gratifying to engage in something that brings both peace and new social connections.
Absolutely. It's given me a sense of peace that's been missing for a while. Every day I'm learning to let go of feeling inadequate.
Letting go of feeling inadequate is a big deal. You're showing so much strength by focusing on self-growth and healing.
Thank you. It's still a work in progress, but having these supportive spaces makes a difference. I suppose I just need to keep reminding myself that it's okay to take things one day at a time.
You're doing an incredible job, Sarah. One day at a time is a perfect approach. You've been making courageous decisions in prioritizing your health, and that truly matters.
I appreciate that. Sometimes I feel lost, but knowing I have a supportive circle helps a lot. Thanks for being here to listen.
Anytime, Sarah. You're not alone in this. I'm here to share this journey with you whenever you need.
Hey there, I just wanted to talk about something that's been on my mind.
Of course, Sarah. What's going on?
Well, lately I've been really immersed in my blog, and just recently got a wave of positive feedback from my followers.
That's amazing to hear! You must be thrilled. How does it feel getting that encouragement?
It truly is uplifting. I was really anxious about how my experiences would resonate with others since I've always struggled with opening up.
It's very brave of you to share your journey. It sounds like you’re finding a meaningful connection through your writing.
Yeah, the feedback has helped validate my feelings and given me a new sense of purpose. But, honestly, I didn't expect it to affect me this deeply.
It's quite natural to feel touched when people respond positively to something so personal. Have you been finding fulfillment from this new avenue?

Definitely. It's very different from the kind of feedback I get at my office job. There, I often feel under-valued, whereas, with the blog, it feels like people actually care about what I have to say.
I'm glad you're finding an outlet where your voice is being heard. That kind of recognition is important. How does this fit with everything else you've been managing?
It's been a bit of a balancing act. Painting and attending art classes have provided a creative escape, but the stress from previous career paths and relationships sometimes cloud my progress.
It sounds like you're juggling quite a bit. It's inspiring how you're incorporating these positive activities into your life despite past challenges.
Thank you. Reflecting on past struggles, like the panic attack at work and issues with Jack, has shown me just how crucial it is to prioritize my mental well-being.
It's crucial to take those lessons to heart. You're making those experiences meaningful by using them to guide your choices now.
I believe so. Honestly, starting therapy and exploring my interests in painting and writing have been essential steps for my growth.
And it sounds like you're taking proactive steps. What do you see as your next focus with all the new insights you're gaining?
I’m thinking more about where my writing might lead and exploring more about self-expression. I’d like to find ways to deepen my connection with people who resonate with my story.
That's a powerful direction, Sarah. Your willingness to share and connect can surely inspire others and foster even stronger connections.
I'm hopeful that it will. I’m also considering doing a series of posts dedicated to managing everyday anxieties, as I have come along in learning to cope.
That sounds like a wonderful idea! Helping others through your experience can be incredibly rewarding and meaningful.
Thank you. You've been really supportive along the way. It’s been wonderful having someone to talk things through with.
Hey Sarah, I saw your recent blog post about your journey. How have things been going since patching things up with your partner?
Hi! Thanks for checking in. Things have actually been better. We had a really good talk, and it felt like we cleared the air. But honestly, I'm still a bit anxious about balancing everything.
It's great to hear about the positive conversation with your partner. Balancing everything can be tough. What's been most on your mind about it all?

I guess it's the fear that things might not last. We've been here before, and I'm worried the issues will come back. Plus, with taking a sabbatical and focusing on my writing, everything feels uncertain.
It sounds like there's a lot of change happening right now. It's understandable to feel anxious about the uncertainty. How have you been finding the sabbatical so far?
It's been a mix. On one hand, it's liberating to have time to focus on myself and my hobbies like painting and writing. On the other hand, not having the structure of work is unsettling.
That makes sense. It’s a big adjustment to shift from the usual work routine. Have you found any activities that help ground you?
Yes, painting has been a big help, and I've been attending the art class I mentioned before. It’s been nice meeting people who share similar interests.
That’s wonderful to hear! Art can be such a powerful outlet. Have you gotten to create anything you’re particularly proud of recently?
I actually painted something for my partner. It was inspired by one of our favorite places to visit together. Giving it to them felt like a small step to solidify our relationship again.
That sounds like a beautiful gesture, and a meaningful way to express your feelings. How did your partner respond to the painting?
They loved it! It sparked a really heartfelt conversation about the things that matter most to us. It was therapeutic in a way.
I’m so glad to hear that. It sounds like you’ve both come a long way in your communication. What are your hopes moving forward with this new chapter?
I hope we can maintain this level of openness and avoid slipping back into old patterns. I'm also hoping to keep up with my writing and maybe share more on my blog.
Staying open sounds like a strong foundation to build on. And your blog is such a great platform to share your experiences. Have you already thought about what you might write next?
I'm thinking about exploring the theme of resilience and how art can be healing, especially how painting has been for me. It's a topic I'm passionate about.
That sounds like a powerful theme. Your story could really resonate with many people. It seems like you’re finding ways to channel your experiences positively.
Thank you. I'm trying my best. Just need to remind myself that progress takes time and setbacks are part of the process.
Absolutely. It's all about taking things one step at a time. You're doing amazing, Sarah. I’m here if you want to talk more about any of it.
I really appreciate that. It’s comforting to know I have support. Thank you for always being there to listen.
Hey, so last night was a bit emotional for me.
Hi Sarah, I'm here for you. Do you want to share what happened?
Yeah, I spent New Year's Eve with Mark. He's finally out of the hospital and it just felt like such a fresh start for him.
That sounds like a significant moment for both of you. How did it feel seeing him out and about again?
Surreal, to be honest. Mixed emotions, really. I was so relieved, but also nervous about how he’d manage.
It's normal to feel that way. How is he doing now that he's out?
He's doing okay. Taking things slow, which is good. We had a long talk about the future and it made me think about my own journey.
It must have been an enlightening conversation. How do you feel about your own journey right now?
I feel hopeful, but also a bit scared, you know? Like there's all this potential but also the fear of falling back into old patterns.
That makes sense. Change can be daunting, especially when you’ve worked so hard to get where you are. What are you scared of most?
Mostly that I'll lose sight of my progress and get overwhelmed again. It's been a tough year.
You've overcome so much this past year, Sarah. It's understandable to worry about setbacks, but you've also proven your resilience.
Thanks for saying that. I think being around friends like Mark helps remind me of what's important.
Absolutely, having supportive relationships is key. How do you plan to maintain this positive momentum?
I'm trying to focus on my blog and my art. Both have been such great outlets.
That's wonderful. Your creativity seems to be a crucial part of your healing process.
It really is. And the support from my blog followers has been incredible. I never expected it to grow this way.
It's amazing how sharing your journey can touch so many. Plus, you're not just helping yourself but others too.
True, although sometimes I wonder if I'm doing enough. Especially when it comes to supporting friends like Mark.
Being there for your friends is already a lot. It's important to remember your well-being too.
Yeah, you're right. I guess balance is something I'll always need to work on.
And that's okay. Life's a journey, isn't it? Learning and evolving as we go.
Absolutely. Thanks for listening. I feel a bit lighter now.
Anytime, Sarah. You're doing great. Just remember to take it one step at a time.
I will. Here's to a hopeful new year!
Here's to hope! Take care and talk soon.
Will do. Thanks again!

turns.content: Hello. I wanted to talk about my academic pressures.
Hi there. What academic pressures are troubling you today?
Just lots of classes and expectations. Especially with group projects.
Needed someone to talk to about my stress and workload. I don't know what to do with these horrible group members.
I see. It sounds like being in the group project is especially stressing you out. Would you say that's pretty true?
Yes. I have roughly 3 different classes all requiring a group project.
I totally understand. When I was in school I remember being stressed out when we had mandatory group projects as well. Having to deal with others can be a bit stressful at times.
I agree. I also just don't know which project to proritize
I hear you, it sounds like you have a lot going on.
Yep.
What should I do to relax my mind?
Have you thought about seeking advice from a close friend or family member?
Not yet, I am scared to tell my family, considering that they view academic success heavily
With friends, most are busy with their own struggles and I don't want to be bothering them as much
I see, it sounds like you are dealing with your academic pressures all on your own right now then?
Totally. Feels pretty tiring and heavy
Is there possibly a school councilor you could seek advice from?
Maybe, but it feels scary and very awkward to seek them
I hear you, it's definitely not for everyone.
thank you for understanding and talking with me
Of course! We all need an ear to listen once in a while :)
It really helps to get this off my chest
I'm so happy to hear that, it sounds like this was something building up. It's always good to let things out in one way or another.
ya it does help
Is there anything else you would like to talk about today?
Nothing really.
Thanks for the conversation!
Okay, and of course! I'm glad I could help.
hi there! how are you feeling today?
i feel depressed
i'm sorry to hear that. is there a specific reason you are having these feelings?
i feel alone. i feel like i do not have anyone to talk to when it comes to my emotions.

I understand. I have been feeling quite lonely too, I find myself feeling lonely at work and struggling to find someone I trust to talk to about these emotions. Do you have a friend or family member that you trust who might understand some of these feelings?
i do have a few friends that i think i can talk to about how i am feeling however the thought of them being too busy with their work is what prevents me from reaching out to them.

I understand. Correct me if i'm wrong, it sounds like you're nervous to open up to these trusted people because you think they might be distracted by their work to provide the empathy you need and fully understand how you are feeling. Does that sound right?

you know i think that you are right about this. it has always been difficult for me to open to others even with those that have been there for me when i needed someone. i feel like a mix of emotions nervous but at the same time wanting to reaching out for help

I understand these feelings very well. Sometimes, my fear overshadows my want for help. I find it easier to open up to others through writing rather than face to face. Have you considered putting your feelings in writing and opening up to trusted friends and family in this way?

i have been writing for a while but due to my emotions i have stopped writing like i used to. when i did write i did notice a change in my feelings it became more positive and less depressed. now that i stopped writing its like i went back into depression

It sounds like writing your feelings down helped you greatly in the past. May I suggest going back to writing and even letting someone you trust read what you have written down to understand how you are feeling?

yes, writing has been a huge help for me. I would take your suggestion and begin writing again to feel better. and i have let others read what i wrote and they have said it has helped them get over their depression and helped them understand me more
That's great! I am glad to hear that you will begin writing again. Thank you for opening up to me about your feelings. How do you feel about the solution we have come to today?
now that i was able to talk about how i feel with you and you giving me a useful suggestion i feel less depressed and feel motivated to write again. your help has been really helpful for me
That's wonderful! I appreciate your honesty about how you are feeling. I am proud of you for seeking help. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?
thank you so much for helping me. and that is all that i would like to discuss. you have been a big help for me

I am glad I could be here for you! I am hoping you continue to feel better and your writing helps to work out these feelings.  Thank you so much for being open with me. I hope you have a fantastic rest of your day! :)
thank you. hope you enjoy your day
Hi, How are you?
I am the youngest of 5 siblings and I feel all most days now because of my parents
It sounds like you're having a hard time feeling like you have your parents' attention, is that right?
Not their attention, but more on their expectations on me
That sounds frustrating, I'm sorry
Do they do or say anything specific that makes you feel those expectations?
Yes, its more on comparing me to the children of their friends. They always say why don't I have a better job or even plans on marrying rich. Stuff like that is very frustrating
They also expect me to take care of them financially soon, I'm just starting my adult life I want to enjoy it
That sounds very frustrating. I think if I felt those kind of expectations I would be anxious.
Do you feel comfortable talking to them about your feelings?

I'm so sorry to hear about your friend. That must be really hard to process. Do you want to talk more about it?
Yeah, it's just...she've always been there for me, especially through the whole thing with my ex and when I was struggling at school. It feels surreal not being able to support her now.
It sounds like they mean a lot to you, and not being able to be there for her must be really tough. It’s understandable to feel overwhelmed.
Exactly. And it's like all these emotions from the past are surfacing again - the argument with my parents, the panic attacks, the trust issues with my professor. Everything seems to be piling up.
It’s okay to have all these emotions. You've been through a lot recently. How are you managing to cope with everything?
Well, I'm trying to stick to some of the things my therapist suggested, like journaling and mindfulness exercises, but sometimes it feels like I’m just going through the motions.
Journaling and mindfulness can be great tools, but it’s also okay to not have it all figured out right now. Are there moments where you feel a bit more at ease?
Maybe when I'm writing, or when I'm engaging with the online writing community. I get what it feels like to be overwhelmed creatively and emotionally.
That's wonderful to hear. It’s important to have spaces where you feel understood and supported. What’s been inspiring your writing lately?
I haven’t been writing as much because of the writer's block, but the supportive messages from the community have been motivating me to start again, even if it's just jotting down ideas.
It sounds like you're slowly finding your way back to your passion, which is amazing. Give yourself time and space; creativity can be a healing process too.
True. I guess I just need to be kinder to myself. It’s just hard when everything feels so uncertain and unstable.
It makes sense to feel that way, given everything you’re dealing with. Remember, it's okay to reach out to your support system whenever needed.
Thank you. It’s reassuring to know I can share this with you. I guess I just needed to talk it out without judgement.
I'm always here for you, Taylor. You’re doing your best, and that’s more than enough. How about we plan for some self-care activities together soon?
I’d really like that. Maybe a virtual writing session or just a chat would be nice. I really appreciate your support.
That sounds perfect. Let's plan something soon. Remember, you’re not alone in this. Anytime you need to talk, I’m just a message away.
Hey, are you around? I could use someone to talk to.
Hi Taylor, of course I'm here. What's on your mind?
I've just been feeling really anxious lately. I had this realization that I have no idea where I'm going with my studies.
I'm sorry to hear that, Taylor. It's completely normal to feel uncertain about the future. What's been the most challenging part for you?
I think it's the feeling of being stuck. I mean, I'm supposed to be excited about creative writing, but I just feel... lost.
Feeling stuck can be tough. Have you talked to anyone about how you're feeling?
Not really. I tried talking to my professor, but our relationship is strained. It’s hard to trust his advice.
That sounds frustrating, especially when you don't feel supported. What happened?
Well, after failing the mid-term, I put in so much effort to improve, but my grades still slipped. It's like nothing I do is enough.
It's so tough when efforts feel unrewarded. I'm proud of you for trying so hard, though. You deserve credit for that.
Thank you. It just feels like everything's coming down at once—my writing, my studies, and even my relationship with my ex.
You've been through a lot recently. How are you coping with everything?
Honestly, I don't know. My friend's hospitalization was another big hit. I feel so helpless.
I'm really sorry to hear about your friend. It's okay to feel overwhelmed with everything going on.
Thanks. It just feels like I'm constantly worrying, and the future seems so uncertain.
Uncertainty can be scary. Have you found anything helpful in managing these feelings?
I've been trying to write again, but it's hard to get past this block. The online community has been supportive, though.
That's good to hear. Sometimes sharing with people who understand can help. Maybe focusing on small writing goals could be a start?
Yeah, I guess taking it slow might lighten the load. It's just hard accepting that progress takes time.
It's definitely tough, but small steps can lead to big changes. Have you considered speaking more with your therapist about these feelings?
I think I will. She was really helpful last time with the self-worth issues. I need that perspective again.
It sounds like a good plan. It's important to feel supported as you navigate through these challenges.
Thanks for listening. I feel a bit lighter just talking about it.
Anytime, Taylor. Remember, you're not alone in this. Take things one day at a time.
Hey, I wanted to talk if you have some time.
Of course, Taylor. What's been on your mind lately?
Well, I recently participated in a poetry slam. It was quite a new experience for me.
That sounds exciting! How did it go for you?
It went surprisingly well! I mean, I was really nervous at first.
That's totally understandable! Performing can be nerve-wracking. How did you manage those nerves?
I just kept telling myself to focus on the words and the message I wanted to convey.
That's a great strategy. Sounds like you were really in the moment.
Yeah, and when I finished, the applause was unexpected. It boosted my confidence so much.
Wow, that must have felt amazing! How are you feeling about it now, a few days later?
Honestly, it's a mix of pride and a bit of self-doubt. Like, was it a fluke?
I hear you. It's normal to question yourself sometimes, but remember how powerful that moment was.
True. I guess it's just hard not to compare myself to others who've been doing this longer.
It's easy to fall into that trap, but your journey and experiences are uniquely yours.
Thanks, I needed to hear that. I think the poetry slam reminded me of why I love writing.
That's wonderful to hear. You have so much passion, and it shows. Embrace it.
I will. It's been tough lately, especially after struggling with direction in my studies.
I remember you mentioning that. How are things going with your studies now?
Still figuring it out, but the poetry slam was a reminder that I can achieve things I set my mind to.
That's the spirit! And don't forget, it's okay to take your time to find your path.
I appreciate that. I guess I'm learning to be more patient with myself.
Patience is key, and you're doing great. Just keep moving forward at your own pace.
Thanks for the support. It really means a lot.
Anytime, Taylor. You've got this.
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Taylor. What's on your mind?
I got this opportunity to co-author a short story for a college magazine.
That's fantastic news! How are you feeling about it?
A bit unsure, honestly. Part of me is excited, but another part is scared.
It's completely normal to feel that mix of emotions. What about it feels scary?
I guess it's the pressure. I don't want to disappoint my co-author or myself.
Pressure can definitely be intense. Remember, they chose you for a reason. You have talent and a unique voice.
Yeah, I know. I keep thinking about the writer's block I had earlier though.
That was a challenging time, but look how far you've come since then. You even enrolled in that creative writing workshop and it seems to be helping.
The workshop has been great. It reminded me why I love writing. I'm just scared of losing that creative spark again.
It’s understandable to worry about that. But remember, creativity isn’t constant. It ebbs and flows, and that's okay.
That's a comforting thought. I guess I just need to trust the process more.
Exactly. Trusting yourself and the process is key. And don't hesitate to lean on your online writing community for support if you feel stuck.
They have been a great support in the past. I should definitely reach out more.
Yes, they can provide so much inspiration. And remember, you've dealt with similar feelings before, and you managed them well.
True, I did get through it. I just need to keep believing in my abilities.
Absolutely. You've shown so much resilience. You've got this, Taylor.
Thanks for listening. I feel a bit more confident now.
I'm glad to hear that. Remember, I'm here whenever you need to talk. Good luck with the story!
Thank you! I’ll definitely keep you updated on how it goes.
Hey, do you have a moment? I really need to talk.
Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
It's Nate again. He reached out and wants to meet up.
Oh wow, that must have been unexpected. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly? Conflicted. Part of me thinks it's a bad idea, but there's another part that wants closure.
It makes sense to feel torn, especially after everything you've been through with him. Have you thought about what you might say or ask if you do meet up?
Not really... I mean, there's a lot to unpack. I don't even know where to start. Plus, there’s the whole thing with my studies being a mess lately.
It sounds overwhelming. Balancing academics and these personal feelings can be a lot. Remember just to take things one step at a time. Maybe making a list of points you want closure on might help?
That's a good idea. I suppose if I had a clearer picture of what I need closure on, it'd be easier to navigate the conversation.
Exactly, it can help keep the conversation focused on what's most important to you. How are things going with your writing and school? Are you getting support from your professors or peers?
The writing's been better since I found that supportive community. The college magazine project keeps me busy, but school overall... It's still a struggle, especially with grades slipping.
It's great to hear about your progress with the creative writing project. Hopefully, things will stabilize with academics too, but remember it's okay to seek extra help if you need it.
Yeah, I should probably reach out to my professors. I just hate admitting that I’m struggling, you know?
Admitting you're struggling takes strength. No one expects you to handle everything perfectly. Have you found your chats with your therapist helpful in this regard?
Definitely, talking things through with my therapist has been invaluable. She’s helped me see that it’s okay to ask for help, but old habits die hard.
Old habits can be persistent, but you're making progress, and that's what counts. Maybe soon, you'll find it a bit easier to reach out when you need.
I hope so. Thanks for being there and listening. I really appreciate it.
Always here for you, Taylor. Remember, you’re doing your best, and that's enough.
Hey Taylor! How are you doing today? How's everything at the writing retreat?
Hi. It's been a whirlwind, honestly. It's both exciting and emotionally challenging.
That sounds intense. What's been the most challenging part for you so far?
I guess it's dealing with so many thoughts about my future and my self-worth. The retreat's really brought that into focus.
It's completely normal to have those feelings, especially with everything you've been juggling. What does the retreat involve?
Well, we have workshops during the day and writing prompts in the evening. It's structured, but also very introspective.
Sounds like a great opportunity for reflection. How's it been helping with your writing, especially after the writer's block?
It's interesting. I've started to write again, more freely. But sometimes I still feel like I'm not good enough.
I remember you talking about feeling like an impostor after seeing your peers succeed. It's tough, but every writer has their unique voice.
Yeah, I try to remind myself of that. I did have some confidence after the poetry slam, but it fluctuates.
Confidence can be such a fickle thing, especially after setbacks like with your ex and classes. Do you think the retreat is helping you focus on what truly matters to you?
I think so. I'm recognizing how much writing means to me beyond grades or accolades.
That's powerful, Taylor. Reconnecting with your passions sounds like a huge step forward. Have you been able to enjoy some of the small victories during your retreat?
Yeah, there are moments when I read back what I've written and I actually like it. It feels rare but rewarding.
Those moments are incredible! They're a testament to your growth and talent. What about the people at the retreat? Have you connected with anyone?
I've met some amazing fellow writers. It's nice to share our struggles and triumphs. It makes me feel less alone in all this.

It's great to hear you're building connections. You're never alone in this; we're all rooting for you. Anything specific that you've learned or any piece of advice that resonated with you during the retreat?
One thing that stood out was the idea of writing for myself first before thinking about how others will perceive it. It relieves a lot of pressure.
That's such a valuable insight. Prioritizing your own voice over external validation is key. How's it affecting your approach to writing going forward?
I think I'm starting to trust myself more. There's still fear, but I'm learning to confront it rather than avoid it.
Confronting fear is a big deal. Remember your worth and the journey you've overcome to get here. Do you have any goals or plans after the retreat?
I want to finish the short story for the college magazine and maybe explore more poetry. Both give me joy, and I want to hold onto that.
Those sound like wonderful goals. Stay connected to what makes you happy, and I'm confident you'll do great things. Anything else on your mind?
Just working on being okay with mistakes and self-doubt. Thank you for listening—it means a lot.
Always here to listen, Taylor. Keep going, and remember you're doing better than you think. Reach out anytime you need to talk.
Thanks. I will. Take care!
Hey, I talked to my siblings today, and it felt really different, but in a good way.
That’s wonderful to hear, Taylor! How did that conversation come about?
I guess I was feeling overwhelmed with everything—school, writing, just life—and I needed someone to turn to. They've been really supportive lately, and I felt I could open up to them.
It sounds like reaching out to your siblings was a brave step. What did you talk about, if you don’t mind sharing?
We talked about all the pressures I've been feeling with my studies and how I've been questioning my direction. I also brought up how the argument between Mom and Dad affected me.
Those are heavy topics to tackle. It’s great you could discuss those feelings with them. How did they respond?
They were really understanding and just listened without judging. My older brother even shared some of his experiences about feeling lost during college.
That connection must have felt comforting. It’s important to know you’re not alone in feeling this way.
Exactly. It’s been hard to shake off that imposter syndrome, especially when I compare myself to everyone else.
Comparison can be tough, but you have your own unique journey and strengths. What did they say about the imposter syndrome?
They reminded me of the successes I've had, like the poetry slam and co-authoring that story. They encouraged me to focus more on my achievements.
That’s such a positive reminder. It’s easy to overlook our accomplishments amid challenges. How does it feel now, after having that conversation with them?
I feel lighter, I think. Like a weight has been lifted. I’m still figuring things out, but it helps to know they’re there for me.
I’m glad to hear it’s made a difference. Do you think this will change how you approach things moving forward?
Definitely. I want to be more open and not keep things bottled up. I’ve learned it’s okay to ask for help.
That’s a powerful realization, Taylor. Remember, reaching out shows strength, not weakness. You deserve support on this journey.
Thank you. I’ll try to keep that in mind, especially when things get tough. It’s nice having people who remind me I’m not alone.
You’re never alone, Taylor. I’m always here to listen, too.
Hey, are you available to chat? I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed.
Of course, Taylor. I'm here for you. What's been going on?
Well, I had a talk with my mentor today about career prospects, and it left me feeling uneasy.
That sounds tough. Do you want to share more about what made you feel that way?
Yeah. It just feels like everyone else has a clear direction in their careers, and I'm still unsure about mine.
I can understand how that would feel overwhelming. It's okay to not have everything figured out yet. You're still exploring.
But it feels like time is running out, you know? I have friends already in internships or job offers lined up.
It's natural to compare yourself to others, but remember that everyone's journey is different. You're making progress in your own way.
I guess you're right. I just can't shake off this feeling of anxiety and self-doubt, especially after my struggles this past year.
You've been through a lot. With everything from the exam pressure to your friend's hospitalization, it's normal to feel this way.
True. And then there's the whole situation with my ex, which is still lingering in my mind.
That added pressure must be really challenging. Have you thought about setting boundaries for your own well-being?
I’ve been trying. Sometimes it works, but other times, it feels like everything just piles up.
It's important to be gentle with yourself. You've taken positive steps like the poetry slam and the creative writing retreat.
Yeah, those did help boost my confidence somewhat. I felt more like myself during those events.
That's great to hear. Maybe focusing on activities that bring you joy and fulfillment could help you rediscover your path.
I think I need to reconnect with my passion for writing. It's been such a constant in my life.
Writing sounds like a wonderful outlet for you. Don't hesitate to lean on your creative community for support and inspiration.
Absolutely. They've been a great support system for me. I'll make more time for writing.
That sounds like a positive step forward. Remember, you're not alone in this. You have support from your siblings, too.
Yeah, our relationship has improved a lot recently, and it feels comforting.
I'm really glad to hear that. Family is such an important part of our support network.
Thanks for listening. I feel a bit clearer about what I need to prioritize.
I'm always here for you, Taylor. Take things one step at a time and prioritize what makes you happy.
I will. Thanks again. This chat really helped.
Anytime. Reach out whenever you need a friendly ear.
Hey Taylor, how are you doing today? I heard you had a chat with some old friends recently.
Hey! Yeah, I did. It was actually really helpful. They gave me some great advice about my career path.
That's wonderful to hear. What kind of advice did they offer that resonated with you?
They suggested that I focus more on my creative writing skills and consider turning it into a more serious career option, perhaps even beyond college.
That sounds like a great idea, especially given how passionate you are about writing. How do you feel about that possibility?
I'm excited but also a bit nervous. It feels like there's a lot to live up to, and I worry about not being good enough.
It's completely normal to feel that way when considering a major life change. Remember when you participated in the poetry slam and how rewarding it felt?
Yeah, that was an amazing experience and gave me a lot of confidence. I guess I need to hold onto that feeling.
Exactly. You've achieved so much already. It's important to trust in your abilities and keep pushing forward. Have you thought about how to move forward with this advice?
I'm considering taking another creative writing workshop and maybe a retreat. I want to focus on refining my skills and finding my voice.
That sounds like a perfect plan. Exploring workshops and retreats could really help you grow. Plus, you've had great support from your online writing community before.
True, they've been super encouraging and it's nice to have a space where I can share my work without judgment.
Absolutely. Having a supportive community is invaluable. Also, don't forget the positive impact your siblings' support had on you recently.
Yeah, they've been great. It's nice to know that I have people who believe in me, even during tough moments.
You're surrounded by people who care about you and want to see you succeed. Have you shared your career aspirations with them?
Not yet, but I think I should. They might have insights or even know someone who could help me further.
That's a great idea. Your family's advice could be really beneficial. How are your feelings towards your academic struggles now?
I still feel a bit anxious, but I think focusing on writing might alleviate some stress by giving me direction.
Absolutely, having a clear path can really help ease anxiety. Remember, it's okay to take things one step at a time.
Thanks. I really appreciate your support. It helps to talk things through and get my thoughts organized.
I'm always here to listen and help where I can. Keep believing in yourself, Taylor. You're capable of amazing things.
Thank you so much. I'm feeling more optimistic about the future now.

turns.content: How are you today?
I'm doing pretty good.
I'm glad to hear you're doing well in these trying times.
Yah they are very difficult.
How have you been managing everything?
Fine I've been pretty much just trying to go out as little as possible and stay safe.
Same here, it's a tough time to do that after doing it so long. Especially with the holidays coming up.
Yes I would have to agree.
Are you in close proximity to your family?
Yeah I'm staying with them for the holidays and then going back home in January.
I imagine that can create some stress?
No not really it's all good over here.
Well I'm glad to hear it, sounds like you've been managing pretty well then.
Yes because I am on winter break now.
I assume that means you're in college then? So the stress of finals is over now?
Yes I am. And yeah I just finished finals.
That's good, I hope they went well for you.
They did. Some were hard, but at least they're over now.
Yes, now you can relax and spend time with your family without the added stress.
Yes, exactly.
Well I hope you and your family enjoy the holidays and stay safe.
Thank you, you too.
Thanks so much!
Are you with family?
Yes, just my immediate family.
Oh that's good. Staying safe.
Absolutely, the best thing we can do right now. Even though it's kind of a bummer.
Yeah, hopefully things will go back to normal soon.
I hope so too, this has been such a crazy year.
I agree.
Hi, what I can help you with today?
Hi
I had problems in the past and somehow right now
What sort of problems were in your past and now?
I loved physics and I decided to attend university, but soon after I slowly lost my interest and became unmotivated
What was happening in your life that made you lose interest?
Actually the professors and the class atmosphere was the reason, and of course the quality of teaching
so I started to skipping the classes and failing
It sounds like that is a lot of reasons to be stressed. Have you spoken to a school counselor?
Yes lots of stress and pressure. I did not, because we didn't have such things or at least I wasn't aware
But nobody even pointed that why I'm failing, they just didn't care
I agree it is a lot of pressure, but do not let bad teachers deter you. I would reach out to a school counselor and let them know your situation. Every school must have one.
Also, physics is a difficult course to study, but if you chose it, that means you have a very strong mind.
I loved physics a lot more than now, but what's the point of studying when the teachers are pulsing you not to study! (because of the quality of teaching)
I hope there was someone, but I don't think we have a counselor
More reason to speak to a school counselor or school administrator. We need to provide help to students, not have bad teachers deter them.
Yeah, same with me! I wish I could attend a better univeristy
What made you choose this particular university you are at?
I didn't have another choice but this
Have you looked into other Universities for the possibility of transferring
Hmmm, actually I didn't think about this option
Just think about what you want in a good university and research from there
Yeah, I should do it
Thanks for the talk
you've been more helpful than my teachers!
You're welcome I hope you find the perfect university for you
Thanks, I wish  you luck in your future endeavours
Bye then ; )
Goodbye
Hello. Is anyone there
Hello. How are you today?
I'm doing good. I need some advice
What can I help you with?
Lately, my friends started to make jokes about my face being ugly. They even called my face as flat as a pan! What should I do? I see them everyday on the bus
Have you tried confronting them and asking why they are being bullies?
I did and they respond by saying that they are just joking and that I'm handsome. But it's starting to get on my nerves because it's all they make fun about every time they see me!
I'm sure you are very handsome! They could just be jealous.
Haha I would hope so
Still though, it makes me want to avoid them when I go to school on the bus
What do you think I should do then?
I understand, school was tough for me too.
I suggest you tell them to knock it off or you can sit somewhere away from the bus.
Should I just beat them up with my backpack
No, beating them up will only get you in trouble and that won't help.
There's another bus route. Should I just take that instead
I think that could be a good idea if it's not too far out of your way.
I think I will. Their comments make me very insecure
You could also tell a teacher what is happening. They will help you out.
I bet you are handsome! Don't let it get to you.
The teacher would probably make fun of me!
Thanks it's hard to look in the mirror now
Try to tell yourself you are good looking and deserve good things to happen every morning! Look in that mirror and tell yourself good things.
I'll try to be positive for once.
Do you believe working out will help
Working out will help a lot! When I was feeling down on myself I decided to go to the gym three times a week. It was a great confidence boost.
Awesome. I will start to take care of myself and not worry about others then.
That sounds like a fantastic idea.
Hey Nick, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey... I've been feeling pretty down recently.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
