That sounds very promising. How do you feel about this new opportunity and having a mentor involved?
Cautiously optimistic, I guess. But I also find myself worrying about whether I can trust things to go smoothly this time.
It's only natural to feel wary after what you've been through. But having someone experienced on your side can really help.
True. I just really hope this could be the turning point I need to get back on track, both personally and professionally.
It sounds like you're taking all the right steps. Your health is a priority and finding a reliable mentor can be a great advantage.
Thank you for saying that. It makes me feel a little more confident about facing the challenges ahead.
Absolutely, Jessica. You've been through a lot, and it's okay to take each day as it comes. I'm here anytime you need to talk.
Thank you! I really appreciate having someone to confide in, and it helps me feel less alone in all of this.
Hey Jessica, how are you doing today?

I'm sorry to hear that. What's been going on lately?
I recently went to a financial planning seminar. It made me realize just how unprepared I am in managing my business finances.
That sounds like it could be quite eye-opening. What part of it concerned you the most?
The seminar highlighted how important it is to have a clear financial strategy, and I'm not sure I've been doing enough in that area. It's made me anxious.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Sometimes, awareness can be daunting. It seems like you've already taken a significant step by attending the seminar.
That's true. I just wish I had done it sooner. You know, with my past experiences and the business challenges I've faced, I think I've been in a bit of denial.
It's natural to feel that way, especially with everything you've been through with the drop in sales and other stressors. But remember, it's never too late to start making positive changes.
Thanks, it helps to hear that. I sometimes feel like I'm playing catch-up, especially after the partnership that fell through and the account discrepancy.
You've had a lot on your plate, and it's okay to feel like you're catching up. But you're also resilient, and taking these steps to grow your understanding shows your commitment to your business.
I appreciate that perspective. I've also been trying to implement that wellness routine we discussed, and I think it has helped a bit with managing stress.
That's great to hear! Every little improvement counts, especially when you're juggling so much. How's your sleep been with the new routine?
Honestly, it's gotten a little better. It's a work-in-progress, but I definitely feel less exhausted.
That's a positive sign. Even small improvements are progress. It's important to keep focusing on those elements that help you recharge.
Absolutely. I think working with the mentor might also help. They offered some practical advice that I plan to implement.
Having that mentorship can make a big difference. It sounds like you have some strong support in place, which is fantastic.
Yes, their guidance is really reassuring. It's comforting to know I have a resource to turn to when things get tough.
Having a reliable support system can really alleviate some of the pressure. Remember, you're not alone in this.
Thank you. I really needed to hear that today. Sharing these feelings makes them seem a bit less overwhelming.
I'm glad you reached out and felt comfortable sharing with me. You're doing an amazing job, step by step.

turns.content: How may I help you?
Hi I am feeling quite sad today.
Ohh, sorry to hear that. Any partucular reason?
Yes I feel like my friends just don't care about me much at all.
You saying that your friend does not care about you any more. Is that correct?
Yes, when we get together all they want to do is talk about themselves. When I raise something that is bothering me they just ignore what I say and go back to what they want to talk about.
That's not good. You must be feeling left out.
Yes I feel left out and unsupported by them.
Any particular reason they are doing such thing?
Well I think they don't care about me and are just selfish about their needs.
In that case, should you consider them as your friends?
Well they are the only friends I have and I have known them a long time. Do you think I should stop being friends with them ?
If someone is not friendly they are not real friend. You need to find someone who will stand by you no matter what..
Oh well that makes me feel sad too.  I will be saying goodbye to some long friendships. Do you think that is the only answer ?
Ok.. how about hosting them in your place for a gettogether..
Ok how do you think that would help me ?
They might open up if you are hosting .. people are generally nice to the host..
Yes that is true, it's a good idea.  I could also take the opportunity to tell them how I am feeling.
Good.. let's try that.. Anythign else I could help you with?
No you have been very helpful and I feel much better now I have a plan of action to address my problem. Thanks.
Thank you .. have a good day.
Yo
Hi, how are you doing?
I am decent. I am here because my friend talks way too much on the phone, and it frustrates me.
They never want to hang up, and the talk can literally go on for hours.
It sounds like it would be quite frustrating for your friend to talk way too much on the phone.
No, he loves it! I'm the one who hates it.
My goodness! How do they respond when you ask to end the conversation?
I tell him, but he just doesn't get it. Or, he says he understands, but then just goes back to talking!
Or, he may finally end the talk, but the next time we talk, he will just do it all over again!
I wonder what it would be like for him if you hung up the phone even after he said he still wanted to talk.
Wow--that does sound annoying that he will repeat the same pattern the next time.
He will literally talk up to 10 minutes without letting you have a word in. As far as that advice, I have hung up, but he gets extremely offended easily.
That sounds really difficult if he gets offended so easily. I find it hard to talk to some of those kinds of friends.
I'm at my wits end. I tell him all the time. "You talk too much. You gotta stop talking at me. You gotta give the other person a turn. You gotta respect other's time."
What do you get out of the friendship with this other person?
Well, I've been friends with him for a long time. He's funny and can have interesting perspectives on things. Also, we have done a lot together in the past.
That sounds like a lot that the two of you have been through. Were there other times that your friends was more equally responsive or attuned to you in conversations?
Oh, yes, I have other friends in conversations who can take turns and understand the concept of time just fine.
I just don't know what to do about this guy in particular. I still want to be his friend, but he just doesn't change.
I wonder if there is anything nice you could do for yourself when you are talking to him that would make it easier to talk to him.
Do you think I should just have a timer that goes off at 1 minute and let it beep in his face if he goes on for too long to train him like a monkey?
I can see that you are feeling upset and angry when he talks so much and that is totally understandable.
I just need a method. Talking to him is just not working.
He is hard to condition.
Would it hurt his feelings to use a timer like that? It may for some other people.
Yea, but I might be able to slip some humour in there to take the edge off because it is so silly.
Humor is really helpful for a lot of people.
Any other ideas?
Sometimes, people draw or do something else distracting with their hands when talking to someone who dominates the conversation.
So your option is to start just doing something else when he is talking? He might get the message in a subtle way?
Sometimes that is a less offensive way to retrain someone who is being obnoxious or dominant and yet who is easily offended. And, it can help preserve your sense of being grounded.
The strategy works well for me with some of my family members who seem like they will never change. But, with distraction, I enjoy them all the more.
This is true, and it isn't bade advice. Haha! That is funny. Yes, maybe I should find something to carry around with me that I can enjoy.
I don't really like to draw...
Is there anything else that you like to do that would be distracting while also letting you somewhat participate in the conversation?
Yes, perhaps I should just use the internet when he starts talking too much.
I have a phone.
That sounds really helpful. Sometimes people also play phone games or with a fidget spinner. I like your idea of looking on the internet.

This solves the problem in person, but it doesn't solve the talks over the phone, but it has been 15 minutes now and this has been helpful enough. Thank you for your solutions. You have been very supportive and kind to me
I don't want to take up any more of your time. It has been a good conversation.
You are very welcome. I wish you all the best!
Goodbye. You as well.
Bye!
Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How's everything on your end?
Hey, not too great to be honest. I tried opening up to my friends at the gathering I hosted, but it didn't go as I hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that, Jimmy. It sounds frustrating. Do you want to talk more about what happened?
Yeah, I felt like I was finally ready to share some personal stuff, and it seemed like nobody wanted to listen or take it seriously.
That must have been really tough, especially when you were putting yourself out there. How did you end up feeling after that?
I felt pretty down. It was like my feelings didn't matter to them, and it made me question if they really care about me.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It sounds like you were looking for some support from your friends.
Exactly. I just wanted someone to hear me out and maybe offer some advice or comfort.
Feeling dismissed by friends could be really disheartening. Have you experienced anything like this before with them?
Not really. That's why it was kind of a shock. I just didn't expect it from them.
That makes it even harder when it's unexpected. Was there anyone at the gathering who you felt did listen or understand?
I think one of my friends was trying, but got caught up in someone else’s conversation. It wasn’t like they ignored me on purpose.
It sounds like they had a lot going on at the time. But still, it's important that they realize how that affected you.
Yeah, I hope I can talk to them about how I felt. I'm just not sure how to bring it up without making it awkward.
It's definitely a delicate subject, but expressing how you feel is also important. Maybe you could start by mentioning how much their support means to you?
That's a good idea. I guess I could tell them that it would really mean a lot to me if they could be there for me when I need it.
That sounds like a thoughtful way to start the conversation. Remember, real friends will want to support you when they know something's up.
Thanks, I really appreciate that. It helps to talk it through and feel a bit more prepared.
Anytime, Jimmy. I'm here for you if you need to chat more. You're doing great by taking the steps to communicate how you feel.
Thanks, it means a lot. I'll let you know how it goes.
Hello
Hi there I was hoping you can help me.
Sure. What can I help you with?
Well you see I am heartbroken and I can't seem to move on from a previous relationship, and its been over two years. Do you have any advice?
I’m understand how hard ending a relationship can be.
What do you find is the hardest thing for you each day. That is, where do you find it hardest to move on?
Well I would say mentally because I frequently think about her and constantly have memories throughout the day. Also when i hear a certain song or see a restaurant it makes me think of her.
Memories are a blessing and a curse. Are the memories and thought you are  having positive or negative?
They are a mix of both because at one point they were positive and now when I think about it, it brings me down in a negative way.
What have you done in the past to help you move on from a break up?

It’s hard when we have various emotions. These memories being more negative are hard to cope with. In my experience, if I rethink memories regarding relationships which tend to bring me down in way that is a learning experience, I feel more empowered.
Yeah I agree that's what I have been doing too, and it's nice to know that you do the same.
In my past I have been able to try and look at each  relationship as a chance to grow. To figure out what worked with that person and what didn’t. I have them used this as a tool for the future.
That's a good way to look at it.
You are making good steps to rethink the situations. Is there anything else contributing to the heat rack you still feel?
Heartbreak
Well I have also not met anyone since and fear that I will not fall in love again.

That is difficult. I understand how it feels to be lonely. Something I’ve done when I’ve felt that way was to learn to fall in love with myself. I like to do self care and make time for things I might not have time for if I were in a relationship.
hmm interesting I have never thought about falling in love with myself..maybe I will give it a try. Thanks.
It’s so important to love yourself. Self love breeds confidence and confidence is not only attractive, but powerful in so many ways
I appreciate the feedback and support, you have helped me take the next step to move on with my life.
I’m glad I could help. You will overcome this.
Thank you and hope to talk to you again. Have a good night.
You too.
Hey George, it's really good to catch up with you. How have you been?
Hey Jimmy! It's great to hear from you. I've been doing alright, just busy with work. How about you? What's been going on?
Well, things haven't been the easiest lately. I feel like I'm kind of stuck in a bit of a rut.
I'm sorry to hear that. Want to talk more about what's been going on? I'm here to listen.
Thanks, I really appreciate it. You know, it's been tough feeling like my friends don't take me seriously when I try to open up.
That sounds frustrating and isolating. It's important to feel heard and supported. What happened?
A few weeks back, I hosted a gathering and tried talking about some things that have been on my mind, but it seemed like no one was really listening.
It must have felt pretty hurtful to be ignored, especially when you needed support.
Yeah, it really was. It's made me hesitant to bring up how I'm feeling again, even though I know I need to talk about it.
It's understandable to feel that way after being dismissed. Have you thought about what you'd most like to share?
I guess there's a lot, but lately, I'm really worried about my job. I've been having trouble managing things because of... well, an alcohol problem.
That's a big thing to carry alone. Admitting you have a problem is a significant first step. You're really brave for acknowledging it.
Thanks. It took me a while to come to terms with it. I'm worried if I don't get a handle on it, I might lose my job.
That concern is definitely valid. Are there specific steps you're thinking of taking to manage it?
I've actually started seeking professional help. It's scary, but I feel a bit more hopeful having someone to guide me.
That’s really proactive, Jimmy. Having professional support can make a huge difference. How are you finding it so far?
It's early days, but I feel like I'm starting to understand more about why I drink the way I do. It's hard work, though.
Facing these things can be intense, but it sounds like you're gaining some valuable insights. That's progress.
Yeah, I guess so. It's nice to hear that from someone else, though. It reinforces that I'm doing the right thing.
Absolutely, you're on the right path. Remember, it's okay to lean on friends for support too. I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Thanks, George. It means a lot to have you in my corner. I'll definitely reach out more often.
Anytime, Jimmy. We'll get through this together. Just take it one step at a time, and keep focusing on the positive changes you're making.

I get that. You've had a lot on your plate. What's been going on?
Well, I went to an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting for the first time yesterday.
That's a huge step, Jimmy. I'm really proud of you for taking it. How did it feel?
Intimidating, honestly. Walking in there, not knowing anyone, feeling vulnerable... it wasn't easy.
I can only imagine how tough that must have been. But you did it, and that says a lot about your courage.
Thanks, George. I kept thinking about that day at the gathering when I tried to talk to everyone but felt ignored.
I remember you mentioning that. It must've been so frustrating to feel unheard by people you consider friends.
Yeah, it was. I guess that's part of why I pushed myself to try something different, like the AA meeting.
That makes sense. It sounds like you’re finding new ways to address things that were weighing you down.
Yeah, I hope so. I just worry about the process, you know? What if I can't handle it?
It's normal to feel that way, Jimmy. Recovery is a journey, not a sprint. It's okay to have doubts.
I appreciate that. I do want to keep going, but the fear of failing is there.
Fear is natural, but remember you've already taken the first step. You have the support to go through this.
Thanks, that helps. The people at the meeting were welcoming, which made a difference.
That's really good to hear. It's important to feel supported and understood in a group like that.
Yeah, it felt different from trying to talk with my current friends. I think I need this new beginning.
It sounds like you're on the right path, Jimmy. I'm here for you, whatever you need.
That really means a lot to me, George. Thanks for being there.
Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How have the AA meetings been going?
Hey there. Well, surprisingly, they've been quite helpful. I met someone there, Bob, who's kind of going through the same issues.
That's great to hear. It must feel nice to have someone who truly understands what you're going through.
Yeah, definitely. It feels different from when I talked to my other friends. They just didn't get it, you know?

Exactly. With Bob, I don't feel judged. We can share our stories, and it's like this unspoken bond.
That unspoken understanding can be so powerful. Have you been able to open up more because of it?
A bit. It's scary, but I’ve been sharing more of my feelings, and it feels freeing somehow. The fear of being judged or not being taken seriously is starting to fade.

Yeah, definitely. I've started to recognize some patterns in my behavior and why I turned to alcohol. It's frightening to see, but it’s the first step, I guess.
Acknowledging those patterns is a huge step. It's brave of you to face those issues head-on.
Thanks. I just sometimes worry if I’m too late, you know? That I might lose everything.
It's normal to feel that way, but you’re taking action now, and that’s important. It's never too late to make a change.
Yeah, you're right. I guess I just have to keep reminding myself of that.
Absolutely. And remember, you're not alone in this. Bob and others at AA are there for you, and so am I.
I appreciate that. It's comforting to have a supportive net. I need to hold onto that.
You're building a strong foundation, Jimmy. Just keep taking it one day at a time.
Thanks. It helps to break it down like that. I’ll try to focus on each day and not get overwhelmed.
That sounds like a solid plan. You've got this, Jimmy. Remember, progress is progress, no matter how small.
Thanks a lot. Your words mean a lot to me right now. I’ll keep them in mind.
Anytime. I'm here whenever you need to talk. Keep me posted on how things go, okay?
I will. Thanks again, really. I'll talk to you soon.
Hey Jimmy, how are you doing today?
Hey. It's been a rough day, to be honest.
I'm here for you. Do you want to talk about it?
Thanks. Yeah, I had a disagreement with my manager at work today.
That sounds frustrating. What happened?
We didn't see eye to eye on what should be prioritized. It just made me anxious.
Conflict like that can be really stressful. Did you get a chance to express your perspective?
I tried, but it felt like he wasn't really listening. It reminded me of when I felt ignored by friends before.
I remember you sharing that experience at the gathering you hosted. It's tough feeling sidelined.
Exactly. It feels like no matter where I turn, I'm not being heard.
It's disheartening when communication doesn't feel effective. Have you been able to talk to anyone else about this?
I did mention it to my new friend from the AA meetings. It helps having someone who gets the struggle.
It's great that you have that connection. How are things going with AA?
It's been eye-opening and comforting, but the work stress isn't helping.
Balancing everything can be challenging. Would you consider discussing this with your manager again with maybe different strategies in mind?
I've thought about it. Maybe writing down my points beforehand could help.
That sounds like a solid plan. It might help make sure you’re heard.
Thanks. I just need to find the courage to approach him again.
You have that courage, Jimmy. Remember how you stepped up to attend those AA meetings?
Yeah, you're right. If I did that, I can do this too.
Absolutely. You're stronger than you realize. I'm here to back you.
Thanks for saying that. It means a lot.
Anytime. Let me know how it goes, okay?
I will. Thanks again for listening.
Always here for you, Jimmy. Take care.
Hey Jimmy, how are you holding up today?
Honestly, not too good. Just got hit with a job performance warning, and it's stressing me out.
I'm really sorry to hear that. That sounds incredibly tough. Do you want to talk more about what led to it?
Yeah...it's mostly my attendance. You know how work has been, with the disagreements and stress?
I remember you mentioning some tension at work. How are things with your manager now?
It's been a bit strained. The disagreement over prioritizing tasks hasn't really helped.
That's understandable. It's hard when there's ongoing stress at work. Have your AA meetings been helpful in managing some of these feelings?
They have, to some extent. Meeting people like Bob has been supportive, but it's still a struggle sometimes.
It's great that you found someone you can share with at AA. Every small step counts in the big picture.
True, but when I got this warning today, it felt like everything crashed down on me.
Getting a warning can be really overwhelming. It's okay to feel that way. Do you think talking to HR or finding mediation could help?
Maybe. I guess I'm just scared of more confrontations or things not going my way.
It's completely normal to feel apprehensive. What about focusing on things you can control right now? Like setting a plan to improve attendance?
That's a good idea. I could try creating a schedule or setting reminders. It might keep me more organized, too.
That sounds like a solid plan! Little changes can make a big difference. I'm here if you want to brainstorm more ways to manage stress at work.
Thanks. Just having someone to talk to already eases some of the pressure.
I'm glad to hear that. Sometimes sharing the load makes it much lighter. Remember, you're not alone in this.
I appreciate it. I should probably talk to my manager soon and address this before it gets worse.
That sounds like a proactive move. Having an open conversation might help clear the air. I believe in your ability to handle this, Jimmy.
Thanks for believing in me. I'm going to try my best.
That's the spirit. Remember to take care of yourself, and don’t hesitate to reach out whenever you need to.
Hi Jimmy, how are you holding up today?
Hey. Honestly, not too well. I had a bit of a slip up recently.
I'm really sorry to hear that, Jimmy. Do you feel like talking about what happened?
Yeah, I guess it's better to talk about it. I was at a family gathering and it just got overwhelming... and I ended up drinking.
Family gatherings can definitely be tough. What do you think made it overwhelming for you?
It was just a lot, you know? Everyone kept asking about my job, and there was a lot of pressure to 'act normal.' I tried to keep it together, but it felt like suffocating.
It sounds like there was a lot of unwanted pressure and it became too much. It’s understandable, given everything you've been dealing with. What did you do after realizing you had relapsed?
Honestly, I felt ashamed. But I reached out to Bob, my new friend from the AA meetings, and they were pretty supportive about it.
That's great that Bob was there for you. How are you feeling after talking with Bob?
A bit better. They reminded me that recovery isn't about being perfect; it's about trying to improve one step at a time.
That's a really healthy perspective. It's important to be gentle with yourself through this process. How else can I support you right now?
I'm just trying to figure out how to communicate better with my manager and deal with work stress. Bob suggested a couple of strategies.
That's a good step. Improving that relationship could lessen some of your stress. Do you feel like talking about those strategies?
Bob mentioned setting clearer boundaries and maybe considering mediation if things don't improve. It's nerve-racking, but I know I have to do something.
Those sound like constructive steps forward. It’s about finding what works best for you. Do you have anything else in mind that might help ease the stress?
I've also thought about re-evaluating my workload to manage it better. Maybe take some time to plan rather than just react.
Planning sounds like a promising approach. It might give you more control over the situation. Remember, you're making progress, even on the hard days.
Thanks. I needed to hear that. It's easy to get lost in the mistakes and forget about the progress.
We all need reminders sometimes. You're not alone in this, Jimmy. Anytime you want to talk, I'm here.
I appreciate that. I think I'll take things one day at a time and reach out whenever I feel stuck or overwhelmed.
That sounds like a solid plan. Don't hesitate to lean on your friends, your AA support group, or me. We believe in you.
I will. Thanks again. It really helps to have someone to talk to who understands.
Hey Jimmy, how are you holding up today?
Not great, honestly. I had a fallout with George yesterday about my drinking.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like it was a tough conversation. Do you want to talk about what happened?
Yeah, we were talking about old times, and then out of nowhere, he brought up my drinking and how it affected my relationships.
That must have been really hard to hear, especially from someone who's been a part of your life for so long.
It was. I know he's concerned, but it felt like he was just pointing fingers rather than trying to understand where I'm coming from.
It's difficult when the people we care about struggle to see the full picture. Do you think there’s more to the discussion that bothered you?
I think I just felt cornered. I've been working so hard to manage my alcohol issues, attending AA, making new friends like Bob who gets it, and fighting my depression.
You're doing a lot to manage things, Jimmy. I can see how much effort you've been putting into this. Does George know about the progress you've been making?
I thought he did. I’ve tried to share some of what I'm going through, like when things didn't go well at a party I hosted a few months ago, but maybe I haven't been clear enough.
It can be hard to express everything we're going through, especially when others have already formed their own opinions. How do you feel about reaching out to him again?
Part of me wants to, but I'm scared he'll just dismiss my feelings again. It's frustrating because I'm trying so hard not to fall back into old habits.
That frustration makes a lot of sense, given how much you're trying to change. Maybe explaining your journey more deeply to George could help him understand better.
You’re probably right. It's just tough when I feel like everyone around me sees only the mistakes.
It's true that others often focus on our past, but remember, Jimmy, you know your progress best. You're the one living this journey daily.
Thanks, that means a lot. I've been trying to not let the fear of judgment drag me down, but it's a struggle.
You’re incredibly strong for pushing through those fears. Focusing on the support you're getting from places like your AA friends can be a good way to stay motivated.
Yeah, Bob has definitely been helpful. It's great to have someone who truly understands what it's like.
Absolutely. It sounds like having Bob and the AA meetings as a support system is making a positive impact on you.
It is, and I need to keep reminding myself of that. I know that’s crucial for my mental health.
Taking care of your mental health is so important, especially with all you've been managing. Keep focusing on those positives, Jimmy. You're doing an amazing job.
Thanks for saying that. I really needed to hear it today.
Anytime you need to talk, I'm here for you. You're not alone in this.
I appreciate that. It’s comforting to know I have someone I can reach out to.

sessions.topic: emotion and mood, treatment and help-seeking

turns.content: Hi Jimmy, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. I'm trying something new with mindfulness and meditation.
That's interesting! What made you decide to explore mindfulness and meditation?
I just felt really overwhelmed after everything that happened recently. My anxiety has been through the roof.
I can imagine. It sounds like you've been through a lot. How have the mindfulness exercises been for you so far?
It's still new, but I think it's helping a bit. I can, at least, find moments of calm when I focus on it.
That's great to hear, even small moments of relief can be a huge step forward. Have you found any particular techniques that work well for you?
Guided meditations seem to work best, especially those focusing on anxiety. It's like having a support system even when alone.
It sounds like a very constructive approach. Have your interactions with Bob from the AA meetings been helpful as well?
Yeah, Bob's been really supportive. It feels good to have someone who truly gets it.
That's fantastic, having someone to share and talk to can make a huge difference. How have things been at work since last we talked?
Work has been tense. Got a warning over attendance, which just adds to the anxiety, you know?
That sounds really tough, especially when you're dealing with so much. Are you finding any ways to manage the stress related to work?
I'm trying to focus on what's directly in front of me and not let my mind wander. But at the same time, those past arguments with my manager still haunt me.
It's understandable. Past conflicts can linger, but it's great that you're focusing on the present tasks. Maybe addressing these feelings with a professional could also be beneficial?
You might be right, seeking professional advice could help make sense of this tangled mess.
Absolutely, a therapist could offer strategies specifically tailored for you. How do you feel about that idea?
It feels daunting, opening up to someone new, but necessary if I want to move forward.
It's okay to feel that way, and taking that step shows real courage. I'm here to support you no matter what you decide.
Thank you. It really means a lot to have your support through this.
You're welcome, Jimmy. Remember, it's all about small steps. Keep focusing on those calming moments and you'll make progress.
I will. I'll let you know how things go with the meditation and maybe even therapy.
I'd love to hear about it. Let's catch up again soon, whenever you feel like talking.
Sounds good. Thanks again for being there.
Hey Jimmy, how are you holding up lately? We've missed you on the group chat.
Hey. I've just been spending a lot of time at home. Had a rough weekend, to be honest.
I'm sorry to hear that. What happened over the weekend?
I kind of shut myself in and just binge-watched TV. Felt too worn out to do anything else.
That sounds really isolating. I've had weekends like that too. Do you feel up for talking about what's been wearing you out?
Yeah, it's just been a lot. I had an argument with George last week, and I feel like everything's just piling up.
I'm sorry about the argument. You've worked hard at this. What happened with George, if you don't mind sharing?
It was about my drinking. I had a slip-up recently, and he didn't take it well. I know he's concerned, but it felt like he wasn't hearing me.
It's tough when friends don't understand the whole context. It sounds like you're really trying, and this slip-up might have felt discouraging.
Exactly. I’ve been going to AA and trying mindfulness, but sometimes the stress just gets to me. It's not easy.
Absolutely, it's definitely not easy. You've taken big steps like AA and meditation, and those are major achievements.
Thanks for saying that. I just wish I didn't feel so alone in all this sometimes.
It's understandable to feel that way. Have you been able to talk to anyone at AA about how you're feeling?
I've talked to a new friend I made there, Bob. He gets some of what I'm going through, but I guess I still feel distant.
That's good you've got Bob to talk to. Building those connections can help break the isolation bit by bit.
Yeah, it helps. I'm trying to keep moving forward, even though some days feel heavier than others.
Moving forward, even slowly, is still progress. What things have been helping you stay on track most recently?
Meditation’s been a new one. It helps calm the chaos up there, you know? And talking with someone who gets it like Bob brightens things.
That’s great to hear. Those personal insights are valuable. How about getting back to the things you enjoy, like activities that give you joy?
I used to enjoy running. Maybe I can ease myself back into that, start small. It used to clear my head.
That sounds like a wonderful idea. Fresh air and some movement could be really rejuvenating.
Yeah, it could be. I just need to find that drive again. Thanks for listening; it means a lot not to feel judged.
Of course, anytime. You're doing the hard work, and I'm just here to remind you that you're not alone in this.
Hey there, I've been meaning to talk about something that happened recently.
Hi Jimmy, of course! I'm here to listen. What happened?
I went hiking with my friend from AA the other day. It felt really good to be out in nature.
That sounds refreshing! How did the hike go for you?
Honestly, it was invigorating. We climbed a trail in Namadgi National Park. The views were breathtaking.
Namadgi is beautiful! Being out there can be such a great escape. Did it help clear your mind?
Yeah, it definitely lifted my spirits. I've been feeling isolated since the argument with my college friend. The hike gave me some peace.
I'm glad to hear that. It's understandable to feel isolated after a disagreement. Nature has this amazing way of healing.
It really does. Plus, Bob, my friend from AA, was super supportive. We talked a lot about letting go of past grievances.
That's wonderful to hear. Having someone who understands your struggles can be incredibly comforting. How are things with Bob going?
We've been getting along well. It helps that he's dealing with similar issues. We tend to support each other through our ups and downs.
Mutual support can be such a pillar of strength. It sounds like you've found a true ally in Bob.
Absolutely. Having an ally like him makes this journey less daunting. But sometimes, I still feel this lingering anxiety.
Anxiety can be tough, especially with everything you're balancing. Have you been able to use any of the mindfulness techniques you were exploring?
I've tried a few breathing exercises from meditation apps. They help in stressful moments, but I often forget to use them consistently.
It can be challenging to create new habits. Remember, every little bit helps, and it's okay if progress is slow.
Thanks for saying that. At times, I feel guilty for not making faster progress, like with the relapse at my family gathering.
It's important to be gentle with yourself, Jimmy. Relapses are part of the journey for many. You're taking steps forward, which matters.
I know, but it’s hard to shake off the guilt sometimes. I just want to do better.
Wanting to improve is a strong sign of growth. Celebrate the victories you've had, like finding solace in hiking and building stronger connections.
You're right. I'll try to focus on the positive. The hike did give me renewed hope.
Hope is a powerful thing. Keep holding onto it, and remember, you're not alone in this.
Thanks for being here. It helps knowing I have support.
Hey, I could really use someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Jimmy. What’s been going on?
I relapsed again. I feel so frustrated and alone.
I'm sorry to hear that. Relapses can be really tough. What's been weighing on your mind recently?
The isolation is getting to me. Ever since that argument with my friend, I feel like I've lost one of the few outlets I had.
It's understandable to feel that way after a disagreement with someone close. Have you been able to talk to your AA friend about how you’re feeling?
We talked a bit after our hike, but I didn't want to burden them with my issues.
I’m sure they’d understand and want to support you, just like you’ve been there for them. It's okay to lean on friends.
I know. I'm just tired of feeling like I'm not moving forward.
Progress can sometimes look like two steps forward, one step back. You’ve made strides by attending AA and practicing mindfulness.
I guess you're right. I did feel better when I was meditating regularly.
Maybe revisiting those practices could help? They seem to give you a sense of peace.
Yeah, I should try getting back into it. I felt more in control when I was doing it consistently.
You’re strong for recognizing what helps you. It’s okay to need reminders along the way.
Thanks. It’s just hard to shake off the feeling of failure.
Mistakes don’t define you, Jimmy. We all have them. It’s about how you keep going that counts.
I appreciate that. I think I need to reconnect with my other support systems.
That sounds like a positive step. Maybe reaching out to your therapist could provide some guidance too.
I’ll set up a session soon. Thanks for reminding me I'm not doing this alone.
Always here for you, Jimmy. Remember, you've come a long way, and we're all here to help you keep moving forward.
Thanks. I feel a bit lighter having talked this through.
I’m glad to hear that. Anytime you need to talk, just reach out. You've got this.

turns.content: Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How are you holding up lately?
Hi there. I've had a bit of a rollercoaster week, to be honest.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been happening?
Yeah, it's been weighing on me. My college friend reached out and apologized after our argument about my drinking.
That sounds like it might be a step toward healing things. How do you feel about the apology?
It was a relief, but I also feel conflicted. I appreciated the apology, but it brought up a lot of mixed emotions.
It's understandable to feel conflicted. Apologies can be tricky, especially when you've been through a lot. What emotions are you experiencing?
There's relief and hope, but also some lingering hurt and frustration. Part of me is scared of things going back to how they were.
It sounds like you’re protecting yourself and being cautious, which makes total sense given everything. What do you think might help you navigate these feelings?
I'm trying to focus on mindfulness and meditation again. It helped before, but it’s hard to stay consistent when emotions flare.
It's great that you're returning to mindfulness. It can be challenging to stay committed, especially in tough times. How have you been finding it this time around?
Some days it really helps to calm my anxiety, but other days it feels like I’m just going through the motions without really feeling better.
That’s completely normal. Progress isn’t always linear, and every step counts. Have you discussed these feelings with your therapist or at AA meetings recently?
Not really. I’ve been hesitant to bring it up, fearing it might trigger another spiral, but I know I should.
Talking through these experiences can be really relieving and is a good step for moving forward. Do you think you might reach out to your therapist or maybe your AA friend soon?
I plan to. I’m still a bit scared, but I know isolation isn’t the answer.
That’s very brave of you, Jimmy. Remember, it’s okay to take small steps toward recovery. How about setting a small goal, like scheduling a meeting or quick chat with them?
That's a good idea. I think setting a meeting would make it harder to back down.
Exactly, and you don’t have to go through this alone. You have people who care and want to support you. How are you feeling now about the whole situation with your friend, after talking this through?
I feel better. More clear about taking these steps. I guess I’m learning to accept that rebuilding connections might take time.
It’s wonderful to hear you’re feeling clearer. Rebuilding does take time, but you’re on the right path. I’m here if you need a listening ear anytime.
Thanks, that means a lot. I’m grateful for your support.
Hey Jimmy, happy belated birthday! How are you feeling about everything?
Thanks. I guess I'm just feeling a bit down. My birthday made me reflect on things.
I'm sorry to hear that. Birthdays can bring up a lot of emotions. What kind of things have you been reflecting on?
It's just been this overwhelming sense of lost opportunities and thinking about past relationships.
That sounds tough, Jimmy. It's understandable, especially with how complex relationships can be. Is there one particular relationship that feels unresolved?
Yeah, it's been hard getting over my last relationship. I worry that I won't find love again. It's been on my mind a lot lately.
That heartache can be really hard to shake. It makes sense that you'd feel that way, especially when birthdays often make us review our lives.
Exactly. Plus, there’s this feeling that I should be further along in life by now.
It sounds like you're putting a lot of pressure on yourself. What do you think being 'further along' looks like for you?
I don't know... I guess having a stable relationship, doing well at work, and feeling content. I feel like I’m lacking in all these areas.
It sounds like you're experiencing a lot of self-doubt, which is natural. Remember, the path to all those things isn't a straight line.
That's true. Sometimes I wonder if I’m making progress at all. The argument with my college friend didn't help either.
I remember you mentioned that. Have things improved between you two since the apology?
It's been better. We’ve talked it out, but there's still this lingering discomfort when I think about it.
It's understandable to feel that way. Forgiveness is a process, and it's okay to take your time with it.
Yeah, I suppose so. I've been trying to focus on meditation to calm my thoughts.
That's great! You've been through a lot and it's important to find ways to ground yourself. How has meditation been working for you?
It's helpful, but I struggle to focus. My mind keeps wandering back to all these worries.
It's perfectly okay to have those thoughts and feel distracted. It's part of the practice. The key is being gentle with yourself when that happens.
Thanks. I think I need to keep reminding myself to be patient. Sometimes I assume healing should happen faster.
Patience is definitely key. You're already doing a lot by acknowledging your feelings and taking steps to manage them.
That makes me feel a bit better. I guess I’ll just keep trying to take it day by day.
Absolutely. Every small step you take is progress. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.
I appreciate it. Thanks so much for listening and being supportive.
Of course. You're not alone in this. Whenever you need support, I'm just a message away.
Hey, happy Valentine's Day! I finally did it.
Happy Valentine's Day, Jimmy! What did you do?
I went ahead and joined a dating app. It's a bit nerve-wracking, to be honest.
That's a big step! It's understandable to feel nervous. How are you feeling about it now?
I feel a mix of excitement and anxiety. It's been a while since I even considered dating.
Experiencing a mix of emotions is completely normal. What made you decide to take this step today?
Well, it’s Valentine's Day and it's been a tough time with all the reflections since my birthday. I guess I wanted to change things up.
That makes sense. Starting fresh can be empowering. How have your past reflections influenced this decision?
I've been thinking about the missed opportunities and my past relationship. It’s easy to get stuck, but I know I need to move forward.
That's a strong realization. Moving forward can be difficult but also quite rewarding. Are you hopeful about this new journey?
Yeah, I think so. I'm trying to stay optimistic, even though I'm also feeling a bit vulnerable putting myself out there.
Being vulnerable can be scary, but it's also where real connections often start. How are you handling the vulnerability?
I'm reminding myself that everyone feels this way and that vulnerability can lead to growth.
That's a healthy perspective. Have you had any interesting interactions on the app so far?
I’ve only just started browsing, but there are a few people who seem interesting. I haven't messaged anyone yet.
Taking baby steps is perfectly fine. When you're ready, reaching out might lead to some fulfilling conversations.
Yeah, I guess it’s about finding a balance between being open but also careful.
Exactly. It sounds like you're approaching this thoughtfully. How are you balancing this with everything else going on, like work and AA meetings?
I'm trying to keep up with everything. Work is still stressful with my manager, but the AA meetings give me a sense of structure and support.
Having that support can make a huge difference. Do you feel like the AA meetings and your new dating journey are complementing each other?
In a way, yes. AA teaches me to be more present and sincere, which I think will help in dating.
That's insightful, Jimmy. It sounds like you're building a strong foundation for yourself.
Thanks, I hope so. I'm just taking things one step at a time.
That's the best approach. Remember, you’re growing and learning each day. You're not alone in this journey.
I really appreciate your support. It means a lot to have someone to talk to about all this.
Hey George, do you have a moment? Just had a lot going on.
Of course, Jimmy. Always here to listen. What’s been happening?
I finally went on a date with Emily. You know, the one I met online. Feeling kinda hopeful but also really anxious.
Oh wow, that’s great! How did it go? It’s understandable to feel both excitement and nerves.
It went well, I think. We enjoyed each other's company, but I’m scared of messing it up, you know? I kept thinking about past relationships and how they ended.
It’s normal to have those fears, especially after the reflections you had on your birthday. It’s important to be gentle with yourself.
Yeah, on my birthday I was just dwelling on everything I’ve been through. All those missed opportunities.
Birthdays can bring those emotions to the surface. But it sounds like you’re taking positive steps now by putting yourself out there again with Emily.
I guess so. But I'm still struggling with anxiety. What if I end up drinking too much again? I don't want to go down that path.
Your concern shows how committed you are to staying on track. Have you talked to your AA friend or therapist about these worries?
Not yet. I’m planning to see my therapist soon. I did go hiking with my AA friend last month, which helped, but this is different.
That’s good you’re planning to see your therapist. And sounds like that hike was refreshing. Maybe finding outdoor activities regularly could help manage your stress?
I’ve started meditating a bit too, hoping it helps. But it’s just hard when these anxious thoughts take over.
Meditation is a great tool. Remember, it takes time to form new habits. You’re showing strength by acknowledging your worries and seeking help.
Thanks, George. Your support means a lot. I just hope I can balance everything – work, personal life, and staying sober.
It’s definitely a lot to juggle, but you've made progress before, and you will again. Just know you’re not alone in this.
I appreciate that. I need to focus on the positives, like the connection I felt with Emily. Maybe I should tell her about these feelings?
That might be a good idea. Being open and honest could deepen your connection. Plus, it might ease some of your anxiety.
Yeah, you're right. I’ll think about how to bring it up with her. Thanks for chatting, George. It helps a lot.
Anytime, Jimmy. Keep me posted on how things go with Emily and your progress with everything. You’ve got this.
Hey, are you around? I could really use someone to talk to.
Hi Jimmy! I'm here. What's been going on?
It's been a rough day at work. I'm starting to question if I'm even in the right career.
I'm sorry to hear that. What happened today that made you feel this way?
There was just a lot of stress and pressure from my manager. It feels like no matter what I do, it’s not enough.
That sounds incredibly frustrating. Have you had a chance to discuss this with your manager?
We’ve had disagreements before about prioritization, but it doesn’t seem to help.
It's tough when communication doesn't lead to changes. How does it make you feel about your job and overall career path?
Honestly, it makes me doubt if I should even be in this field. It's like a constant weight on my shoulders.
That heavy feeling can be really overwhelming. Does anything about your job still bring you joy or satisfaction?
I used to enjoy the work, especially when I felt valued and part of the team. But lately, it’s just been draining.
It sounds like things have really shifted for you. Was there a particular moment when it started feeling this way?
I think the stress really intensified after the job performance warning. I've been on edge ever since.
Understandable. That warning seemed to impact you deeply when it happened. It's hard to shake that pressure off.
Yeah, and with the recent drinking relapses, I feel like I'm constantly fighting an uphill battle.
I recall how challenging those moments have been for you. But I also know you're strong and have been working on it.
Sometimes I wish I could just start fresh, but I don’t know what else I’d even do.
Starting fresh can be intimidating, but it's also an opportunity. Have you thought about exploring other options or passions?
I’ve considered it. I just worry about the risks and if I'll end up in the same situation eventually.
It's normal to have those concerns, but sometimes taking a step towards change can lead to unexpected positive outcomes.
You're right. Maybe I do need to look into what genuinely makes me happy outside of work stress.
That could be a great start. Have you considered revisiting the mindfulness practices you tried before? They might provide some clarity.
I actually haven't thought about that in a while. It might help me process everything without feeling overwhelmed.
It could definitely offer some peace of mind. Remember, you're not alone in this, and I’m here to support you.
Thanks. It feels good to talk this out and know I have someone to lean on.
Anytime, Jimmy. Keep me posted on how things unfold, whether it's work, mindfulness, or anything else.
I will. I appreciate your support more than I can say.
Hey George, can I talk to you about something that's been on my mind?
Of course, Jimmy. What's going on?
Well, I've been considering moving to Sydney. It's a huge decision for me.
Wow, that's a big step! What made you think about relocating?
I need a fresh start. Things here in Canberra have been weighing me down—work stress, my struggles with alcohol, and this feeling of being stuck.
I can understand wanting to leave all that behind. But are you sure relocation will solve those feelings?
Not entirely, but I've been thinking that a new environment could help me focus on healthier habits and new opportunities.
That's a good reason. Sometimes a change of scenery can bring new perspectives. Have you thought about how you'll manage your support network there?
That's one of my worries. My therapist and AA meetings are here, but I've looked into resources in Sydney.
It sounds like you're planning ahead, which is wise. Maybe reconnecting with new groups could also help.
Yeah, I'm trying to be practical about it. And I'm moving in with a colleague I know from Sydney—Emily. We hit it off recently.
Oh, Emily from your recent date? That seems promising! How do you feel about that?
A bit anxious but hopeful. It's about finding a balance, I guess. I don't want to mess things up again.
It's understandable to be nervous. But you're aware of what you want to avoid, which is a strength.
I try to remind myself of that. It's just hard not to dwell on past mistakes sometimes, you know?
I do, but remember, each day is a new chance to do things differently. How do you feel about your work situation with this move?
I'm actually looking forward to new job opportunities. Canberra was stifling me a bit career-wise.
That's great to hear. Taking control of your career can be incredibly empowering.
Thanks, George. Your support means a lot. Chatting with you helps me sort things out in my head.
Anytime, Jimmy. You've got the courage to face all this, and that's inspiring.
I appreciate it. I'll keep you updated on how the move goes. It feels good to have someone to talk to about this.
Please do. Remember, you've got people who care about you no matter where you are. Don't hesitate to reach out.
Will do. Thanks again, George. It's reassuring to know you're here for me.
Always, mate. Take care and good luck with the move!
Hey Jimmy, how are you doing today?
Hey, I'm feeling a bit off. I took a walk around my old workplace in Canberra and it brought back a lot of memories.
That sounds intense. What kind of memories did it bring up for you?
A mix of good and bad, honestly. I miss the routine, but I also remember the stress and how overwhelmed I felt back then.
It makes sense to have mixed feelings. Have you been thinking about your decision to move to Sydney at all?
Yeah, it’s been on my mind. Part of me wonders if I'm making the right decision, leaving it all behind.
It's natural to have doubts, especially with such a big change. What do you hope to gain from moving?
A fresh start, I suppose. I want to leave behind the stress and the drinking issues I faced here.
That sounds like a healthy goal. How have you been coping with those challenges recently?
I’ve been trying meditation and mindfulness. It's helping, but I still slip up every now and then.
You've been working hard to improve, and that's commendable. Do you feel the change of scenery might help with your healing?
I think so. I need a place where I can focus on becoming the best version of myself without constant reminders of the past.
That sounds like a positive step. How has the idea of relocating affected your daily routine currently?
It’s been a bit unsettling. I've been trying to wrap things up here, but it's hard to leave things behind.
I guess it’s a mix of excitement and anxiety. Have you talked to anyone else about how you’re feeling?
I mentioned it briefly to my AA friend. They understand where I’m coming from, but I still feel quite alone in this.
I'm glad you have someone to relate to, but it's also important to reach out to others, like your therapist, if you need more support.
You’re right. I've been meaning to, but sometimes I just don’t know where to start explaining how I feel.
That can be tough. Maybe starting with how it feels to revisit old places and planning your move could be a good entry point.
That’s a good idea. I just hope moving will give me the perspective and space I need to heal.
It sounds like you’re on the right path by acknowledging these feelings. Remember, it’s okay to seek help along the way.
Thanks, I really appreciate your support. I'll try to keep taking these steps forward.
Anytime, Jimmy. You’re doing great just by being open to change and growth.
Hey, I found something today while packing and it's kind of messing with my head.
I'm here for you, Jimmy. What did you find?
I stumbled upon an old letter from my ex-girlfriend. It brought back a lot of memories and feelings I thought I had moved past.
I can only imagine how overwhelming that must be. Do you want to talk about what those memories are bringing up for you?
It's just… it made me realize how much I've been trying to escape certain feelings instead of dealing with them.
That sounds like a powerful reflection, Jimmy. It’s never easy to confront past emotions. What’s been the hardest part for you about this realization?
It's the regret, I think. Regret about how things ended, and feeling like maybe a part of me hasn’t truly grown since then.
Regret can be tough to sit with. It sounds like you're questioning if you've made the progress you hoped for.
Yeah, and it makes me worry about whether I’ll just repeat my mistakes with Emily or keep stagnating in other parts of my life.
It’s understandable to feel that way given your recent journey. You've been working hard on yourself, though. Remember how far you've come since starting those AA meetings.
True, attending those meetings has helped. It just feels like there’s always this shadow of doubt following me.
Doubt can often linger, but it's also a sign that you're questioning and reflecting, which is a part of growth. Do you think the move to Sydney will help with some of these feelings?
I hope so. I see it as a step towards a new beginning, yet there's a fear that I might carry the same emotional baggage there.
It's natural to be worried about taking your past with you, but sometimes a change of scenery can offer a fresh perspective and reset.
That's what I'm banking on. Just hoping I can leave behind these old habits and finally start anew.
I believe you have the strength to make positive changes, Jimmy. You've shown a lot of resilience already. What’s one thing you’re looking forward to in Sydney?
Probably the chance to reinvent myself, meet new people, and maybe discover parts of Sydney I’ve not considered before.
That sounds like an exciting opportunity. You've got a world of possibilities ahead, and I'll be here to support you along the way.
Thanks, that means a lot. I guess time will tell how things unfold, but it’s reassuring to know I’m not facing this alone.
Absolutely, Jimmy. You’re not alone, and you’ve got a network of support that’s rooting for you. Keep us updated on how things go, okay?
I will. Thanks for listening, it’s helped put things in perspective.
Anytime, Jimmy. Take care of yourself while you’re packing, and remember to take things one day at a time.
Hey Jimmy, how are things going in Sydney so far?
Hi... honestly, it's been a bit overwhelming getting settled into the new job.
I can imagine how challenging that must be, especially with everything else going on. Do you want to talk about what's been particularly tough?
Yeah, I guess the anxiety is really getting to me. I had a panic attack at work the other day.
Oh no, that sounds really tough, Jimmy. I remember you had started exploring mindfulness and meditation; do you think that could help?
I've been trying to get back into it, but it's hard to focus when I feel so on edge.
Understandable. Maybe it might help just to take small steps, like short breathing exercises throughout the day?
That's a good idea. I think I need to break things down into more manageable pieces.
Yes, exactly. It's all about finding a balance that works for you. Have you talked to anyone else about how you've been feeling?
Not really, I kind of feel alone here. I miss my support network from Canberra.
It's tough being away from familiar faces, but I'm here for you, and your friend from AA might be someone good to reach out to.
Yeah, he was really supportive before the move. Maybe I'll give him a call.
Good idea. It might help just to hear a familiar voice. How's the new place otherwise? Any positives you’ve noticed?
The city is beautiful, and I've found a nice park nearby. It reminds me of going hiking with my AA friend.
That sounds lovely. Going for walks there could be really refreshing. Sometimes stepping outside can really clear your head.
I think I'll do that more. I need to find those moments of peace.
Absolutely. It's okay to take time for yourself, especially when you're adjusting to so much change.
Thanks for saying that. Sometimes I forget it's okay to slow down.
We all need reminders. Just take things one day at a time and be kind to yourself.
I'll try to remember that. Thanks for listening; it really helps just to talk it out.
Anytime, Jimmy. Remember, you're not alone in this, and it's okay to reach out whenever you need to.
I appreciate that more than you know. I feel a bit lighter now.
I'm glad. Keep taking those small steps, and you'll find your way. We’re all here cheering for you.
Thanks, it means a lot. I'll keep pushing forward.
Hey, can we chat for a little bit? Something's been bothering me.
Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I heard from Jennifer today. It brought back a lot of emotions.
Wow, that must have been unexpected. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, I'm all over the place. Her reaching out made me think about all the things that didn't work out.
It's understandable to feel stirred up. Have you talked to anyone about this yet?
Not really. It's hard to even know where to start.
Take your time. I'm glad you decided to reach out. What did she say when she contacted you?
She just wanted to see how I was doing and mentioned that she's back in town.
That must have been tough to hear. Did it bring back memories of your time together?
Yeah, more than I expected. It's like all those emotions were just under the surface.
Emotions can be really powerful, especially ones tied to past relationships. Do you think talking to Jennifer might help, or would it be too painful?
I'm not sure. Part of me wants to see her, but another part is scared of going back to that place emotionally.
It's tough to balance those feelings. Listening to your gut is important. How are you managing everything else in Sydney?
It's been a challenge. The new job has been overwhelming, and I haven't really found my footing yet.
Changes like this can be disorienting. Have you had the chance to make any new connections or contacts that might help you feel more settled?
Not yet. I guess I've been pretty closed off since the move.
That's understandable given everything. It might be worth finding a supportive community or group in Sydney, like you did with AA. You've been through a lot and you're doing your best.
You’re right. I just need to remind myself that it's okay to take things one step at a time.
Absolutely. And remember, you're not alone in this. I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Thanks. I really appreciate your support. I’ll try to look into some local groups this week.
That sounds like a great plan. Small steps forward can make a big difference. Keep in touch, okay?
I will. Thanks for listening and for being there.
Anytime. Take care of yourself, Jimmy.

sessions.topic: love and intimacy, emotion and mood

turns.content: Hi George, I hope you're free to chat for a bit?
Hey Jimmy, of course! What's going on?
I've been having a rough patch emotionally. Yesterday, I wrote a letter to my ex-girlfriend. It brought back a lot of memories.
That sounds heavy. What prompted you to write the letter?
We talked recently, and it stirred up old feelings. I felt I needed to get everything off my chest for some closure.
I can understand why that would be important to you. How did it feel writing it all out?
It was cathartic, actually. But at the same time, it made me reflect on a lot of what-ifs and missed opportunities.
It’s natural to reflect on those things, especially when so much has changed since. Did it help clarify your feelings at all?
I think so. I've been feeling a mixture of relief and sadness. Like a chapter is finally concluding.
Endings can definitely feel bittersweet. Have you been able to talk to anyone else about this?
Not yet. You're the first person I reached out to. I thought about talking to Jane, my therapist, but I haven’t made the appointment yet.
I'm glad you reached out. It sounds like it might be a good idea to schedule that session with Jane.
Yeah, that's probably a good idea. I worry that if I don't address these emotions, they might affect other parts of my life.
That's a valid concern. You've been working hard on moving forward, and processing these emotions can only help with that.
Thanks, George. It’s just tough navigating these waters. But talking about it definitely eases some of the burden.
I’m happy to be here for you, Jimmy. Remember, it’s okay to take one step at a time. Have you considered how you'll spend the next few days?
I think I'll try to keep busy. Maybe focus more on my new job in Sydney and make plans to meet with friends here.
Sounds like a solid plan. Keeping active can help manage those feelings of sadness. And it sounds like you do have a support network you're building there.
Yeah, I’m trying. It’s challenging starting fresh, but it’s comforting to know I’m not alone in this journey.
You’re doing great, Jimmy. Just keep reaching out when you need an ear, okay?
Thanks, George! I really appreciate our talks. I’ll try to focus on the positives and keep pushing forward.
Anytime, mate. You've got this. Just take it day by day.
Hey Jimmy, how have you been doing lately?
Hey, I'm okay, I guess. I've started journaling daily. Thought it might help me make sense of everything.
That's a great step. Writing things down can help untangle what's going on inside. How's it been for you so far?
It's been... enlightening, but also a bit heavy. I didn't realize how many emotions I've been bottling up.
I can imagine. Opening that bottle can be tough. Have you discovered anything about yourself through journaling?
Yeah, I've noticed a pattern of avoiding conversations that make me uncomfortable. I guess I've been doing that a lot.
Recognizing those patterns is a big first step. It shows you're gaining clarity. Have any specific situations come to mind?
Well, my recent move to Sydney was partly because I felt trapped by my past here in Canberra. Wanted a fresh start, but I miss some things too.
That makes sense. A change in environment can be refreshing but also difficult. What do you miss the most?
I miss the familiarity and some of my friends. Even George, despite our disagreements. But I can't deny I felt suffocated.
It's understandable to feel torn. Change can bring both liberation and loneliness. Have you reached out to them since the move?
Not really. I guess part of me is scared they won't understand or that things might go back to the way they were.
That's a valid worry. But you've grown, and sometimes revisiting old connections can bring new perspectives. What's holding you back the most?
Aside from fear, it’s the guilt. I feel like I left things so unfinished. Kind of like with my ex-girlfriend.
Those are heavy feelings to carry. I know you’ve written a letter to her. How did that feel, getting things out on paper?
It was cathartic. Very freeing in a way. I realized that closure isn’t just about her, but also about forgiving myself.
Self-forgiveness can be a powerful aspect of healing. It’s wonderful you’re recognizing that. How has this realization impacted your day-to-day?
It's helped me be gentler with myself. I'm learning to accept that it's okay to not have everything figured out.
That’s such an important lesson. Life's unpredictable, and nobody has all the answers. What steps are you planning to take next?
I think I want to reach out to George, maybe have an honest conversation. I’m also thinking of scheduling a therapy session soon to talk through some of this.
That sounds like a promising approach, Jimmy. Reconnecting with friends and seeking professional guidance can provide the support you deserve.
Thanks. I appreciate you listening to me ramble. It helps just to voice these things out loud.
Always here for you. Remember, it’s okay to take things one step at a time. You’re doing great, Jimmy.
Hey George, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Jimmy. What's up?
A lot has been happening lately, especially with Emily. We've decided to become exclusive.
That sounds like a big step! How are you feeling about it?
It's exciting, but honestly, I'm a little anxious too.
Understandable. It's normal to feel both excitement and anxiety with changes like this.
Yeah, exactly. Given everything that's happened over the past year, I'm a bit worried about messing things up.
I get that. You’ve had quite a journey with highs and lows. But you've also been learning a lot, like through your AA meetings and mindfulness practice.
True. Those have helped me a lot. But sometimes, I can't help but think back to my past relationships and where I went wrong.
It’s good that you're reflecting, but don’t be too hard on yourself. Growth comes from experience, even the not-so-great ones.
I've been trying to keep that in mind. Starting the journal has helped me sort through some feelings.
That’s a great tool for self-reflection. Have you shared any of these feelings with Emily?
I have, a little. She's really understanding, which is reassuring. But I don't want to overwhelm her with my issues.
It sounds like you two have a good line of communication. It’s okay to share what you're comfortable with. You're building a partnership here.
You're right. I guess I’m just afraid of getting too comfortable and slipping back into old habits.
That’s a valid concern. But it sounds like you’re more aware now. Awareness is a powerful first step to change.
Definitely. I’ve made it a point to stay connected with my AA friends. They've been great support.
That support network is so important. And remember, I’m always here to listen too.
Thanks, it means a lot. I’m just trying to take it one day at a time.
That’s a great approach. Celebrate the good days with Emily and learn from the tougher ones.
I will. Thanks for hearing me out, George. I feel a bit more grounded now.
Anytime, Jimmy. You're doing better than you think. Just keep moving forward.
Hey Jimmy, how have you been doing lately?
Hi there. It's been mixed, honestly. I had this unexpected encounter recently that stirred quite a bit inside.
Oh? What happened?
I bumped into an old high school friend while walking in Sydney. I hadn't seen them in years.
That must have been a surprise! How did that make you feel?
At first, I felt warmth and nostalgia. It's nice to connect with someone from the past. But it also sparked feelings of loneliness since moving here.
Meeting someone familiar can really bring back memories. It's understandable to feel a mix of emotions. Have you had a chance to catch up?
Yes, we grabbed coffee and reminisced about the old days. It was fun, but it reminded me of some of the friendships I've drifted away from.
It's tough to realize how time changes our relationships. How are you handling those feelings?
I've been journaling about it a lot, trying to process and reflect. It's helping somewhat, but I do miss having deeper connections.
Journaling can be such a helpful tool. It sounds like you're doing your best to stay grounded. Is there any way I can support you right now?
Thanks. Just having someone to talk to helps. I've been trying to meet new people but it's been challenging.
Building new connections in a new city is definitely challenging. Are you finding any places or groups where you might connect with others?
I've been attending new AA meetings here. I did meet a few people there, but it's still early stages for forming deeper bonds.
That's a big step, Jimmy. Being proactive in attending meetings shows your commitment to both your well-being and to connecting with others.
Thanks. Sometimes I doubt myself, questioning if I'm making the right choices. Moving here was supposed to be a fresh start.
Doubts are normal, especially with big life changes. From what you've shared, it sounds like you're making thoughtful decisions on your journey.
I try to. Some days are harder than others, and running into old friends has just stirred a lot inside.
It's a lot to process. If you need to talk through it more, I'm here. You’re not alone in this.
I appreciate that. Really, having someone listen means a lot to me. I'll keep working through these feelings one day at a time.
Absolutely, one day at a time. You've come a long way, and it's clear you're making strides. Reach out whenever you need to.
I will. Thanks for being here for me. It feels good to know someone cares.
Always, Jimmy. Keep taking care of yourself and staying open to the connections you're building.
Hey, I've got some news. I finally got a promotion at work!
That's amazing, Jimmy! Congratulations. How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, it's a mix of emotions. I feel proud, but also a bit nervous.
It's understandable to feel that way. Promotions can come with their own set of pressures. What's making you nervous?
I guess it's the new responsibilities and adapting to this role. After all the ups and downs, I'm just scared of slipping back.
With everything you've overcome, it's natural to worry. But remember, you've shown so much resilience already.
Thanks for saying that. I've been reflecting on how far I've come and those tough times, like adjusting to life in Sydney.
You've taken huge steps, from managing anxiety to building a new life there. How are you handling those challenges now?
I'm trying to stay grounded with journaling and occasional hikes. Emily's support also helps.
I'm glad you have positive outlets and people around. It sounds like you're maintaining a good balance.
Yeah. Speaking of balance, I still worry about past triggers, especially since moving brought back old feelings.
Old feelings can resurface, but don't forget the methods you've embraced to manage them. You're stronger than before.
I appreciate that. I do feel stronger. Sometimes I just need reassurance that I'm on the right path.
It's okay to seek reassurance. Everyone needs it. Trust the journey you're on and the growth you've achieved.
You're right. This promotion is a step forward, and I need to focus on that.
Absolutely. Celebrate your achievements, Jimmy. You've earned it.
Thanks. It's good to have people who remind me of my progress. I really value our talks.
I'm always here to listen. You're doing great, and I'm proud of your journey.
I'm grateful for that. Here's to moving forward, step by step.
Hey Jimmy, how are you feeling after the group session today?
Hey, thanks for asking. It was quite intense. Confronting my feelings about the past isn't easy.
I can imagine it's tough. What did you find most challenging about it?
Honestly, admitting that I still have attachments to my ex-girlfriend. It's hard to let go.
That makes sense. Holding onto past relationships can be really impactful. How are you dealing with these emotions?
I'm trying to journal more, like my therapist advised. There's just so much guilt and sadness I need to work through.
Journaling is a great way to process those feelings. Have you noticed any patterns or insights so far?
Yes, definitely. I've realized I tend to idealize the past, especially when I'm feeling lonely or stressed.
That's a really important realization. It seems like you're making progress in understanding your emotional triggers.
Thanks. I just wish I wasn't so drawn back to those old memories, especially now that I'm in a new relationship with Emily.
It's natural to feel conflicted. You're not alone in feeling this way. Have you been able to talk to Emily about this?
Not yet. I'm afraid it might hurt her or make things awkward between us.
That’s understandable, but honesty is key for a healthy relationship. Maybe you can start by expressing how you're working through old feelings and want to be open with her.
You're right. I think I’ll try to talk to her about it. I know she deserves to know, and it might help me move forward, too.
Absolutely. Giving her insight into your journey could bring you two closer. And remember, your feelings are valid. You're doing the best you can.
Thanks for saying that. Sometimes I feel like I'm failing at moving on, but hearing this helps.
You're definitely not failing. Healing is a process and you're taking the right steps by seeking support and working on personal growth.
I appreciate your support so much. It feels less overwhelming when I can talk about it.
Anytime, Jimmy. You're never alone in this. I'm here whenever you need to talk or just unload your thoughts.
That means a lot to me. I'll keep you updated on how things progress with Emily and my journey to closure.
Looking forward to hearing about it. Take care and be gentle with yourself.
Will do. Thanks again for everything!
