turns.content: Hey Kelly, how are you doing today?
Hey, to be honest, I'm struggling a bit.
I'm here to listen. Do you want to share what's been challenging for you?
It's my thesis. I had a setback recently, and it's just really bringing me down.
I can imagine that must be tough. What happened with your thesis?
I got some feedback that I wasn't expecting. It made me realize there's a lot more work to do than I thought.
That sounds overwhelming. It can be really hard to digest unexpected feedback.
Exactly. I was feeling quite confident before, and now I just feel lost.
It's okay to feel that way. Remember, feedback is part of the process. How are you managing these feelings?
Not too well, honestly. I've been pretty demotivated and haven't been able to get much done.
It's understandable to feel stuck. Sometimes taking a step back can help. Have you tried taking a break from it all?
I've tried, but it's hard not to think about it. It feels like I'm letting myself down.
You're not letting yourself down. You're doing your best under challenging circumstances. Remember when your friend mentioned overcoming similar doubts in his studies?
Oh yeah, he struggled with something similar and he got through it. It took him a bit of time though.
Exactly. Maybe his story can be a reminder that it's possible to bounce back. Have you reached out to your friends recently?
Not recently. Maybe I should. Talking to someone who understands might help.
That sounds like a great idea. And remember, I'm always here for you too. You have support.
Thanks, I really appreciate that. It does help to know I'm not alone in this.
You definitely aren't alone. How about focusing on one small step you can take today?
Maybe I can start by reviewing the feedback more calmly, with a fresh perspective.
That sounds like a constructive plan. Taking it step by step and being kind to yourself on the journey can make a big difference.
I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and helping me process things.
Anytime, Kelly. You’ve got this, even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Keep reaching out, okay?
I will. Thanks again.
Hello
Hi, how are you feeling today?
I'm feeling a bit confused and anxious.
okay, that is valid, do you have an idea what is causing the confusion?

So I've been dating and my parents are aware. But recently after I said I want to go on a trip with my boyfriend, my parents have all sorts of opinions about it. And all their traditional beliefs that I did not know existed are now on the surface and they are kinda forcing me to follow it.
For say they think "bad types of woman" go on trips with their boyfriends and I need to save myself.
They have been guilt tripping me and I feel very confused.
Your feelings are valid and it is okay to feel confused in this situation considering you love your boyfriend and parents
Have you tried discussing with your boyfriend to talk to your parents as a means of reassuring them?
Or getting someone neutral that your parents trust to talk to them?

I have. It's been a long stressful month of discussion. The problem is I don't share their beliefs, and I haven't been really "saving myself". I'm been living away from them for collage quite a while and I've been basically doing stuff that if they found out they would be very upset about.
But I didn't think it bothers them because they never shared any of this.
And they said if I go on this trip I'm disrespecting them and the entire family.
But his parents are totally cool and don't seem to mind.

I get how difficult and upsetting this situation is to you, i have been in a similar situation, however, in my case i took charge of my life, though they are my parents i did what i felt is good for me
Before i continue, do you mind me asking how old you are?
I'm 26
And I see what you're saying.
It's really hard breaking free because they always monitored me my entire life.
I never had a voice for myself. They basically bullied and forced me to do what they wanted.
BTW if you didn't guess I'm their favorite child.
Okay, you are old enough to be away from your parents, i am going to suggest you sitting with them down and having a heart to heart discussion with them
Let them know the consequences of them forcing you, your feelings towards it and how unhappy you are with them restricting you
Should I tell them everything I did that goes against what they believe?
So they know that I don't share their beliefs?
No, i think that should be personal to you, i would not suggest you hurting or making them see you as a disappointment
I am sure you will be fine after discussing with them, they will come around
I guess worst case I won't talk to them for a while : )
Thank you , that helped.
They might be sad and upset now but they will get over it definitely
You are welcome
Have a good one!
You too
How is your feeling now?
I have mixed feelings sad and angry at the same time.
It seems that you are feeling blue and upset by others, right?
Yes. Am sad because I love my mom so much and I never like to get into arguments with her.
From the short conversation, I can feel how sad you are.
Yes. My mom never approves of most of the things I do.
What kind of arguments did you have with your mom?
Like the kind of friends I should have. I believe I have freedom to choose my friends not her.
I had similar situation like yours. My mom did not want me to make friends with some people.
Really? How did you deal with that because for me it makes me angry.
I just had good conversations with my mom to express my thoughts. Did you have a frank chat with your mom to express your concerns?
I try to but it never ends well if I don't agree with her suggestions.
Take a deep breath and it can make you feel better.
What are her concerns about your friends?
OK! I have taken a deep breath.
ok, that's good. tell me more about your mom's concerns of your friends.
She feels that they have some bad influence on me because of their family background. I don't do anything bad with them.
Some of my friends are so good they even inspire me to be better everyday.
My mom told me similar concerns before. It is understandable.
All I need is to find a way to show her that I can make some good decisions as well and that she can trust me to make good friends. I have never gotten into trouble before with my friends
My suggestion is that tell her these facts and she can make a better decision. I think she assumed your friends are bad influencers just based on their family background.
Do I need to buy her a gift or something to let her know I care so as to start the conversation?
Yes, a good idea, it pleases her.
Thank you for your time.
Bye
You are welcome. Hope it will go well.
Hi there, how is this season treating you?
It's alright. Definitely not as cold as last year which is something to be slightly thankful for.
Well let's be grateful for small mercies :). How are you feeling in yourself though? Is there anything you'd like to talk about?
I'm worried about grad school
Ah I am sorry to hear that. Please try not to worry too much as it's a common worry to have. Do you want to tell me the details?

Sure. One of my classes is extremely difficult and the professor has not been responsive at all. The TA is kind enough to make time to help me with homework, but my grades are still not great. It makes me feel really dumb and undeserving to be in that class
So you are feeling as though you are in the wrong place? Do you feel as though you might fail your class completely?

I want to be in the program, it's just that I feel like everyone is so much smarter than me and my performance in that class makes me question my admission into the programs sometimes. When I feel like this after submitting homework, I end up crying because I just want to do well. I enjoy this field, just not this  class in particular.
I'm afraid of failing, but I'm not sure if that should be a concern either. Over the past 3 years, no one has gotten a grade lower than a B.
But do you really think that you would have been admitted to the class if you were not up to the standard? Do you think that maybe most of your classmates are secretly feeling the same?
Sometimes I think about that. At the same time, I feel like it's unfair to compare myself to others.
This sounds like it might be a self esteem issue and not about your grades. I have felt this sort of thing myself and I do know how awful it is to be so hard on yourself.
So what do I do about it? I don't want to keep feeling like this
Have you thought about seeing a therapist? Does your school have any free therapy programmes you could use?

I don't think my school has free therapy programs. I have thought about seeing a therapist but I've heard therapy is very expensive.With student loans, I didn't really put much more research into therapy past hearing about the costs.
A far as I am aware there are charitable organisations which can arrange a few free therapy session for you. Perhaps you could talk to your doctor about it?
I have had free therapy sessions before and I found them very helpful
I think free therapy sessions would be a good place to start
It would help you work on your self confidence and you might find that you are not doing as badly in school as you think you are.
Yeah, there are definitely a lot of other things i'm insecure about
Then I think it is probably just a general self esteem issue and nothing academic!
Anyway it's been really nice to talk to you and I hope that everything goes your way
I think talking about this has helped. I'll do a little more digging. Thank you!
You're most welcome, have a lovely Holiday season.

sessions.topic: social and relationship, emotion and mood, treatment and help-seeking

turns.content: Hey, I really need to talk to someone.
Hi Kelly! Of course, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I got into an argument today with a classmate during our group project meeting. I'm feeling so overwhelmed.
I'm sorry to hear that. It sounds really stressful. What happened in the argument?
We were discussing some decisions for the project, and they just dismissed my ideas completely. It made me feel invisible and undervalued.
That must have been so frustrating. Everyone's contributions should be respected, especially in a group setting.
Exactly. It's like, what am I even doing here if no one will listen.
I can understand why that would make you question your place in the group. Did you manage to express how you felt to them?
Sort of. I tried, but I think I let my emotions get the better of me and it just turned into more arguing. Now I'm worried I've damaged the group dynamic.
Sometimes emotions can take over, especially when you're feeling undervalued. It's understandable. Have you thought about how you might address it with them?
I want to approach them again and explain. But I'm worried they'll just see it as me being difficult or emotional.
It's brave of you to want to reach out again. Maybe approaching them calmly and expressing how the situation made you feel could help clear the air.
Yeah, I think I'll try that. I guess I'm also feeling extra sensitive lately because of that difficult class I'm taking.
Having a tough class on top of this situation is a lot. It's no wonder you're feeling sensitive. How is that going for you?
It's intense. I'm constantly worried I'm falling behind, and it's really impacting my self-esteem.
That's tough. Balancing a challenging class with group dynamics can be overwhelming. Remember, it's okay to feel this way.
Thank you. I've been considering therapy to help with these feelings and to improve my self-esteem.
That sounds like a positive step. Taking care of your mental health is important, especially during stressful times.
I'm glad you think so. I just hope it can help me manage everything better.
I'm confident it will. You're taking the first steps towards understanding and improving your situation, and that's truly commendable.
Thank you. It really helps to hear that and to talk to you.
Anytime, Kelly. I'm always here to support you. You've got this, even when it feels challenging.
I appreciate it more than you know. I guess I'll focus on clearing the air with my classmate and seeking therapy.
That sounds like a great plan. Remember, you're stronger than you think, and you're not alone in this.
Hey Kelly, how are you feeling about your thesis presentation coming up?
Hey! Honestly, I'm feeling pretty anxious about it.
I'm sorry to hear that. What's been making you feel anxious?
I guess it’s the pressure of it all. My thesis is such a big part of my degree, and I really don't want to mess it up.
That makes a lot of sense, it's a big moment. Remember how you pulled through the setback earlier this year with your thesis?
Yeah, I remember. It was tough, but I managed. This feels different, though. It's like everyone will be watching and judging.
Presentations can definitely feel intimidating. It's perfectly normal to feel that way. Do you think there are specific parts of the presentation that you're worried about?
I think I’m most worried about the Q&A part. I'm scared I won't be able to answer their questions, and it will look like I don’t understand my own research.
That’s a common fear. Maybe we can go over some possible questions together and practice? It might help boost your confidence.
That sounds like a good idea. It would help to be more prepared for the unexpected.
Great! And remember, you know your work better than anyone else. It’s normal to get caught off guard, but you've got this.
Thanks, I appreciate that. I guess a part of me also wonders if people will even find my research interesting.
Your research is your unique contribution. It's meaningful and valuable. Don't underestimate the impact it can have.
I try to keep that in mind, but the doubt just keeps creeping in, you know?
I understand. Doubt is tough. Maybe reflecting on why you started this research in the first place might help?
I started it because I wanted to make a difference, and I was passionate about the topic. I guess I’ve lost sight of that a little.
Reconnecting with that original passion can be a powerful motivator. It's still there, even if it feels lost right now.
Yeah, it's reassuring to remember that. I don't want a repeat of that project argument from September either.
I remember you mentioning that. It was a difficult situation, but you handled it well in the end. You grew from that experience.
I did, didn't I? It's just hard to see it sometimes. Thanks for reminding me.
Anytime. You're stronger and more capable than you give yourself credit for. Just take one step at a time.
I will. Thanks for being here and listening to me vent.
I'm always here for you. We can practice the Q&A whenever you're ready.
That’d be great. I’ll reach out soon to set up a time. Thanks again!
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Kelly. What's on your mind?
I had my thesis presentation yesterday, and it didn't go as I hoped.
I'm so sorry to hear that. Can you tell me what happened?
Well, I was really nervous from the start. I tried to stay calm, but I stumbled over my words.
That sounds really stressful. It’s tough when things don’t go as planned.
Yeah, and the Q&A session was even worse. I struggled to answer some of the questions.
It must have been nerve-wracking. But remember, it's okay not to have all the answers. Everyone has challenging presentations.
I know, but I feel like I should have been more prepared. This presentation was really important for my progression.
It's understandable to feel disappointed, especially when you care so much about your work.
Thank you. I just keep thinking about how everyone was watching, and it's hard not to dwell on every little mistake.
It’s natural to replay moments like this, but be gentle with yourself. You're doing the best you can.
I appreciate that. I just wish I could prove that I know my stuff, even if this didn’t show it.
You are knowledgeable, and this one presentation doesn't define your abilities.
It's been a rough month, between this and the argument over that group project.
You've been dealing with a lot lately. No wonder you're feeling overwhelmed.
I guess I just need to find a way to bounce back and regain some confidence.
Rebuilding confidence takes time, but remember how resilient you were after your last thesis setback.
True, I did manage to push through back then. Maybe I can do it again.
Absolutely! Lean on your past strength, and know I'm here for support whenever you need.
Thank you. It really helps to talk it out and get some reassurance.
I'm glad I can be here for you. You're not alone in this.
Thanks. I'll try to keep that in mind and take it one step at a time.
That sounds like a good plan. You've got this, Kelly.
Hey, have a moment to chat?
Of course, Kelly. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling a bit off ever since the presentation.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Do you want to share more about what happened?
The presentation didn't go as I planned, and the Q&A was even worse.
That must have been really challenging. It's understandable to feel disappointed.
Yeah, it's just this lingering feeling of having let myself down.
It's tough to cope with those feelings, especially when you've worked so hard.
My friend invited me to a yoga retreat. I think it's her way of helping me unwind.
That sounds like a thoughtful gesture. A change of scenery and some relaxation could be beneficial.
I'm just not sure if it'll help or if it's running away from my problems.
It's completely okay to take some time for yourself. Recharging doesn't mean avoiding the problem.
I guess a break might give me a fresh perspective when I come back.
Absolutely. Sometimes stepping away helps in seeing things more clearly.
I've been so caught up in trying to perfect everything, maybe too much.
It's easy to fall into that trap. Remember, it's okay to have moments that aren't perfect.
I appreciate you saying that. I tend to forget it's okay to not always meet high expectations.
It's important to be kind to yourself. You've accomplished so much already.
You're right, I need to remind myself of that more often.
Yes, and don't hesitate to lean on your friends or me whenever you need support.
Thank you, I might just take that retreat offer. It could be good for me.
I think that sounds like a lovely plan. Enjoy, and take all the time you need to feel recharged.
Thanks again for listening. It really helps to talk things through.
Anytime, Kelly. I'm here whenever you need to talk.
Talk soon, then. Take care!
You too, take care and enjoy the retreat!
Hey, can we talk? Something's been bothering me.
Of course, Kelly. What's on your mind?
Well, I just got some really harsh feedback on my thesis draft. It just felt like a huge blow.
I'm sorry to hear that. That must be really tough after all the work you've put in. What specifically did your advisor say?
He said that my arguments weren't strong enough and that my writing style was too simplistic. It made me feel like I'm not cut out for this.
It sounds like his feedback hit you hard. Do you think there's anything constructive in what he said?
I guess there could be, but it's just overwhelming right now. I'm trying to see how I can improve but it feels like there's so much to fix.
I understand. It can be overwhelming when the work you care so much about feels criticized. How did you handle it when you had a setback in your thesis before?
Last time, I took a break and tried to approach it with fresh eyes. That helped, but this time feels different. It's so close to the deadline.
Deadlines definitely add pressure. You mentioned a yoga retreat your friend suggested. Have you thought about taking them up on that offer?
I actually have a ticket booked for the weekend. I'm hoping it might give me some clarity and peace.
That sounds like a great opportunity to reset a bit. It's important to take care of yourself during stressful times.
Yeah, I hope it helps. I feel like I need to find that strength again, you know?
And you've shown resilience before, Kelly. Remember your presentation? Even though it didn't go as planned, you pushed through.
I guess you're right. It's just hard when it feels like there's hit after hit.
Life can sometimes feel like a series of challenges, but each one is also an opportunity to grow. You're stronger than you think.
Thanks for reminding me of that. It helps to have someone to talk to.
I'm always here for you, Kelly. Don't hesitate to reach out if you need to vent or just chat.
I really appreciate that. I guess I just need to take this one step at a time.
Absolutely, one step at a time. And remember, it's okay to ask for help when you need it.
I will. Thanks again for listening. It feels good to know someone understands.
You're welcome, Kelly. Take care of yourself, and good luck at the retreat. I'm sure it'll help.
Hey Kelly, how have you been feeling lately? Anything on your mind?
Hey. I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed, honestly. My friend just confronted me about being emotionally distant, and it's been weighing on me.
That sounds really tough. It must have been difficult to hear that from your friend. Do you want to share more about what happened?
Yeah, it caught me off guard. She said I seemed distant and not really present in our conversations. I guess I've been preoccupied with thesis stuff and all.
It's understandable. You've had a lot on your plate with your thesis and everything else. It's normal to feel overwhelmed.
I know, but it feels like I'm letting people down. I didn't even realize how much I've been pulling away.
It sounds like you're carrying a lot of pressure. You're undergoing so much right now, it's okay to not always be fully present.
That's kind to hear. I just don't want to lose her friendship or make her feel like I don't care.
Your friendship seems important to you. Perhaps there are small ways you can show her you care, even when you're busy?
Yeah, that's a good idea. Maybe I can plan something simple but meaningful to show I'm still around for her.
That sounds lovely. Even a small gesture can mean a lot and communicate your care and intention.
I'll think about it. I guess the stress from my thesis is leaking into other parts of my life.
It makes sense. Have you been able to find ways to manage the stress, especially with the feedback from your advisor?
I've tried, but the feedback really shook my confidence. I feel like I'm in a rut after hearing that.
I'm really sorry to hear that. Criticism can be hard to take, especially when it's about something so important.
Exactly. I almost feel stuck, and I'm not sure how to pull myself out and keep going.
It's not easy, but remember that progress isn't always linear. You've overcome setbacks before, like with the group project misunderstanding.
True, I guess I managed to clear things up back then. Maybe I can get through this too.
Absolutely. You've shown strength and resilience before, and you can do it again.
Thanks for reminding me of that. I think I need to be kinder to myself in all of this.
Self-compassion is important. You're juggling many things; it's okay to have these feelings.
I appreciate your support. Talking about it helps, and I'm feeling a bit more optimistic.
I'm really glad to hear that. You'll find your way through this, step by step.
I hope so. Thanks for listening and being here for me.
Anytime, Kelly. Remember, you're not alone in this.
Hey, can we talk? I feel like everything's just piling up on me lately.
Of course, Kelly. I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
It's just been a rough few months. My thesis, my presentation, now a disagreement with Matthew over holiday plans. It's too much.
That does sound overwhelming. You've had a lot on your plate. What happened with the holiday plans?
We were supposed to go to my parents' place, but Matthew wants us to go on a trip with his family instead. I just feel torn.
It's understandable to feel torn between family obligations. It's a tough situation. How have you been handling it?
Not very well, to be honest. I hate conflicts and it just feels like another thing on top of everything else.
It's okay to feel that way. You've dealt with so much this year. How are things with your thesis going?
It's moving slowly. After the harsh feedback, I've been second-guessing everything. My confidence is shaken.
I remember you mentioned how the feedback got to you. It's tough, but you're resilient. Have you talked to your advisor since then?
Not really. I guess I'm avoiding it, afraid of more criticism. But I know I can't avoid it forever.
Avoidance is a common response, but facing it when you're ready is important, too. What about taking the yoga retreat your friend suggested?
I think it might help. I just haven't had the time. Maybe it's what I need to clear my head a little.
Finding time for yourself can really make a difference. It might also help with the situation with Matthew.
Yeah, maybe I'll consider it. I haven't been my best self lately and he's noticed.
It takes courage to recognize and share that. Your emotional distance from your friend earlier shows you're aware of it.
I suppose so. I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of stress and it's affecting everything.
That's a difficult place to be in. It's important to be gentle with yourself and reach out for support when needed.
I'm trying. Talking with you helps, actually. It's nice having someone just listen without judgment.
I'm glad I can be here for you. Remember, you're not alone in this. We'll work through it together, one step at a time.
Hi Kelly! How have you been doing lately?
Hey, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster, to be honest.
That sounds intense! Is there something specific on your mind right now?
Kind of. My professor praising my work was a huge relief, but it's mixed emotions after everything recently.
I can imagine! It must feel good to have your efforts recognized after the last few months.
Absolutely. Especially after the harsh feedback from my advisor not too long ago. It was quite a blow.
That must have been tough. It shows your resilience, though, that you kept pushing through.
Thank you. It wasn't easy, especially with how anxious I felt about my thesis presentation.
It's completely understandable. Presentations can be nerve-wracking, and when they don't go as expected, it feels disappointing.
Yeah, that disappointment was heavy. It sort of spiraled into making me feel distant from friends too.
I remember you mentioning that. It’s hard to balance everything sometimes. Have things improved with your friends since then?
A bit. My friend confronted me about being emotionally distant, which was eye-opening.
It sounds like a tough conversation, but sometimes those are necessary for growth.
For sure. It was overwhelming, but I appreciate having someone who cares enough to say something.
That makes a world of difference, having supportive people around. How are things with your holiday plans?
Well, there was a disagreement with Matthew over the holidays, which added more stress.
Holiday plans can be particularly tricky. Do you feel it's been resolved, or is it still weighing on you?
We’re working through it. We're both trying to be understanding of each other's perspectives.
That's great to hear. Communication is key, and it sounds like you both are committed to it.
Definitely. Having my professor praise my recent work helped remind me of my capabilities.
It's wonderful to hear that. You deserve to feel confident in your achievements.
Thanks. It’s been a journey, but I'm slowly starting to feel more balanced.
I'm really glad to hear that. Remember, it's okay to take things one step at a time.
I'll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and being supportive.
Always here for you, Kelly. Don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need to talk.
Hi Kelly! How have you been doing?
Hey! It's been a mixed bag lately, to be honest.
I get that. Want to talk about what's been happening?
Sure. You remember how I was stressed about my thesis? Well, my advisor's feedback was tough, but I actually got some unexpected support.
Oh, that's interesting. Where did the support come from?
It's from an old college friend I hadn't spoken to in a while. It was surprising but nice.
That sounds wonderful. How did they reach out to you?
They just sent me a message out of the blue, asking how I was doing. It was so random but perfectly timed.
It's amazing how reconnecting with the right people can make such a difference. What did they say that really stuck with you?
They reminded me of how much work I've already done and how capable I am. It was like they saw through my facade and just knew the right things to say.
That sounds like just the boost you needed. How are you feeling now?
I feel lighter, like a weight's been lifted off my shoulders. It's nice to be reminded that I'm not alone.
It's so valuable having someone to remind us of our strengths. Did you get a chance to talk more about what's been on your mind?
Yeah, we chatted for a while. It helped me see things from a different perspective, especially regarding the thesis.
I'm glad to hear that. Seeing things differently can open new paths forward. Have you thought about what's next?
I'm planning to focus on integrating the feedback from my advisor now. I feel more motivated to push through.
That's a great plan. Keep in mind all the progress you've made so far, too. Do you feel like this interaction changed anything else for you?
Yes, it reminded me to seek support when I need it and not shy away from opening up to friends.
Exactly, having a support system is so crucial, especially during challenging times. Is there anything else that's been on your mind?
I guess just balancing everything and managing my time better. But I feel more equipped now to handle it all, especially with supportive people around.
You seem to be on the right path. Remember, you're not alone, and you have people who care about you. Keep reaching out and taking things one step at a time.
Thanks for being so supportive. It really means a lot.
Anytime, Kelly! Keep in touch, and don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need to talk.
Hey Kelly! How have things been lately?
Hey! Things have been a bit of a rollercoaster recently.
I see, what’s been happening?
Well, Matthew organized this surprise date for us recently. It was really sweet.
Aww, that does sound sweet. How did it go?
It went well overall, but I found it hard to fully relax and enjoy it.
That’s understandable. Do you think there’s anything on your mind that’s been making it hard to relax?
Honestly, I think it's a lot of leftover stress from the recent thesis issues.
The thesis stuff sounds really challenging. Was it when your advisor gave you the harsh feedback?
Yes, that hit me hard. Plus, I have ongoing anxiety about the whole project.
I can imagine how tough that must be. Have you been able to talk to Matthew about these feelings?
I mentioned it briefly, but I don't want to burden him too much since he already did so much for the date.
It’s great that he organized that, but remember, he’d probably want to support you through your stressful times, too.
You're right, I sometimes forget that being open is important too. It's just been hard to get past this barrier.
Totally understandable. Have you considered revisiting the yoga retreat or any relaxation methods to help take some pressure off?
Yes, my friend mentioned the retreat again. I think it might be a good idea to go.
That could be a wonderful opportunity to destress and gain some perspective.
I agree. It’s just daunting to step away when there's so much to do, but I know I need it.
Taking care of yourself isn’t taking time away; it’s investing in your wellbeing, allowing you to come back stronger.
Thanks, that actually helps put things in perspective. I should talk more to Matthew too.
I’m glad it helps! Yes, open communication can only strengthen your relationship. You both deserve that.
Definitely. Thank you for listening and being such a great support.
Always here for you, Kelly. Take it one step at a time, and good luck with everything!
Hey, got a moment to chat? There's something on my mind.
Of course, Kelly. I'm here for you. What's been going on?
I just received an internship offer in my field, and I thought I'd feel thrilled, but I'm more confused than anything.
Congratulations on the offer! That's a big achievement. What about it is making you feel uncertain?
I think it brings back the feelings from last year when my thesis presentation didn’t go well. I'm worried I might not be good enough.
That's understandable, considering the challenges you've faced in the past. It seems like those experiences left quite an impact.
Yeah, it's just that every time something positive happens, I somehow focus on the negative 'what-ifs'.
It's easy to focus on potential negatives after dealing with setbacks, but remember how your professor praised your progress recently? That shows your capabilities.
True, the professor's feedback definitely boosted my confidence at that time. Maybe I'm afraid the internship may not live up to expectations or that I may disappoint them.
It's natural to fear the unknown, but it’s also an opportunity for growth. How did you feel when your friend invited you to the yoga retreat? Did it help change your perspective?
The retreat was refreshing. It taught me to be present and not worry too much. I just wish that feeling lasted longer.
It sounds like the retreat had a positive impact on you. Maybe drawing on that experience can help you approach this new opportunity too.
That's a good point. I should focus on the present and take it one step at a time. I just need to believe in myself more.
You have every reason to believe in yourself, Kelly. You've faced challenges before and come out stronger. This could be another step forward.
I guess you're right. I need to remind myself of the strengths I've shown in the past, like handling that group project misunderstanding.
Absolutely! You've shown resilience and problem-solving skills. Those qualities will serve you well in this internship.
Thanks for helping me see things clearer. I think I just needed to talk it out and get some perspective.
I'm glad I could help. Remember, you can always reach out if you need someone to talk to. I'm rooting for you.
Thank you, really. It's comforting to know I have support. I'll take some time to think about it and maybe I'll end up accepting the offer.
Take your time to decide what's best for you. No matter what, you've got this!
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Kelly! What's on your mind?
I just found out that I didn't get the scholarship I applied for.
I'm so sorry to hear that. You must be really disappointed.
Yeah, it's just frustrating. I really thought this would be my chance to ease some of the financial pressures of grad school.
I can imagine. It's tough when you're expecting something that could make life a bit easier and it doesn't come through.
Exactly. And it just feels like a setback after working so hard, especially after everything with my thesis.
You've been through a lot recently, with the criticism on your thesis and the group project issues. It's okay to feel upset about this.
Thanks. I guess I just keep thinking about all the time and effort I put into the application. It feels like it's always something.
Your dedication is amazing, Kelly. Even if this didn’t work out, it doesn’t take away from all the effort you’ve put in.
It's hard to keep that perspective when these things happen back to back. It just adds to feeling stuck, you know?
Absolutely, and it's important to acknowledge that feeling. Have you thought about what you might do next?
I'm trying to keep my options open. There's the internship offer, but I'm not sure about committing to it right now.
It's understandable to feel conflicted. The internship could be a valuable experience, but it's okay to take your time deciding.
I appreciate you saying that. I guess I'll think on it more after this initial disappointment passes.
That's a healthy approach, Kelly. It's important to give yourself space to process everything.
Thanks for listening and for understanding. It's comforting to have someone to talk to about this.
I'm always here for you. Remember, you're doing incredibly well, even if it doesn't always feel like it.
Your support means a lot to me. I'll try to focus on the positives, like how my professor praised my recent work.
That's a great perspective, and it's a testament to your hard work and dedication. You've got this, Kelly!
Hey, I just needed to talk. Things have been a bit of a mess lately.
Hi Kelly! Of course, I'm here for you. What's been going on?
It's Matthew. Our relationship is feeling really strained, and I think it's mostly because I've been so focused on school.
That sounds stressful. Balancing a demanding grad program and a relationship is tough. How are you feeling about it all?
Honestly, I'm overwhelmed. I want to do well in school and work on my thesis, but I don't want to lose Matthew in the process.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Have you and Matthew had a chance to talk about how you're both feeling?
We've talked a little, but it always seems to turn into an argument. It's like we're not hearing each other.
Communication can definitely be challenging during stressful times. Maybe exploring new ways to express your feelings could help?
Yeah, I guess. I've been so worried about my advisor’s comments on my thesis draft, it's like I can’t focus on anything else.
Your advisor's feedback must be weighing heavily on you. It's tough when professional and personal stress overlap.
It really is. And with the scholarship disappointment, it's like everything is hitting at once.
I remember when your professor praised your work not long ago. That was a sign of your capability and hard work. Perhaps remembering those positive moments might balance some of the stress?
You're right. I just wish I could keep that confident feeling longer. It's like life keeps throwing curveballs!
Life can be unpredictable, but you've shown resilience before, especially after your presentation disappointment last October.
I guess I have bounced back before. I just need to believe I can do it again with Matthew and everything else.
You can do it, Kelly. Taking small steps can make a big difference. Maybe find some shared activities with Matthew to reconnect?
That's a good idea. Maybe we could go to that yoga retreat my friend mentioned. It might help both of us relax.
That sounds like a wonderful plan. It’s important to take care of yourself too. You've got this!
Thank you. I feel a bit lighter after talking this through. It's nice to know that I have people who believe in me.
I'm always here to support you. You're stronger than you think, and you’re making really positive steps.
Thanks, really. I’ll try to take things one day at a time and work on better communication with Matthew.
Absolutely. Sometimes small changes can have a great impact. Keep trusting yourself.
I will. Thanks for listening and being there for me.
Hi there.
hi how are you today? How can I assist you?
I'm feeling really stressed. I'm about to graduate from college, but my last two classes are killing me. I keep having dreams that I've been forgetting to go to the class and now I won't graduate.
It's keeping me from being able to concentrate on the real classes.
It seems you are working really hard and in stress due to your classes.
Yes, I am working really hard.

yes, It happen with all human being I believe.

Yes, balancing grad school with our relationship is so hard. And with the internship offer and other pressures... I feel like I'm constantly choosing between my career and Matthew.
That’s a lot to handle. It’s natural to feel torn. Have you had a moment to think about what a good balance might look like for you?

I remember you were really hopeful about that scholarship. It's understandable that not getting it would add to the stress. How are you coping with that disappointment?
I thought it would help ease my financial burden, so now it adds to the pressure. I'm trying to focus on the positives, like my professor's praise, but it's hard.

Remember, you've had some great achievements recently that are worth celebrating. Sometimes starting with small victories can help regain some control and focus. How did you feel when your professor praised your work?
It was definitely a confidence booster! For a moment, I felt like I was on the right path. But these doubts just keep creeping back in.
It's completely normal for doubts to come and go. Progress isn't always linear, and that’s okay. Maybe focusing on setting small, achievable goals could help?
That's a good idea. I think I get caught up in wanting everything to be perfect. Maybe I need to let go of some of that control.
Perfection can be a high bar to set for yourself. It's great that you're considering being more flexible. Is there one small change you could make this week?
Maybe I'll try setting aside specific time for Matthew and limiting my work time each day. I think he’d appreciate that.
That sounds like a wonderful plan, very considerate of both your needs. How do you feel about trying that out?
It feels good to have a plan. I hope it helps balance things a bit more. Thank you for listening, I really needed this.
I'm glad you're finding a direction that feels right for you. Remember, I'm here whenever you need to talk or just vent. You're doing great.
Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
Hello? Anyone there?
Hi sorry
I'm having trouble getting motivated to finish my senior thesis
Ah! I remember my thesis, a lot of work. One thing for certain, I have a lot of pride over my accomplishment, it was well worth it. When is it due?
In about a month.
I'm sure you will be able to finish it, sometimes we find ourselves in a slump and need some fresh air blown our way.
Do you have an advisor who is holding you accountable?
Yes, but I've been really bad about keeping her in the loop. I feel bad when I fall behind, and then I'm fearful of getting back in touch with her.

Whenever I have a large project and lose motivation, I set my goals on paper, then break it down into smaller bites. For example, I will make sure I work one hour on certain days, or call a friend, I generate ideas to keep me on track.

Yes, I sometimes feel guilty and then don't want to face the music, but actually the best thing to do is recognize you are NOT the first person she knows that got behind. So she is surely experienced with people who need some encouragement. She is the BEST person to go to, actually.
That sounds like a good idea regarding putting it down on paper.

It has always helped me. For example, you can break it down into 4 weeks, then each week write your goals -- maybe put call Advisor or go stop by every week, but I would put that first for the first week.

Then as you check off items, you will see you are moving, even if at a snail's pace, you are moving, and that always encourages me. Sometimes I do not realize how much I AM doing, until I see it on paper. Paper doesn't lie, but my emotions sometimes cloud my thinking.
My other problem is that I'm a perfectionist. I tend to over-analyze and get bogged down, especially when doing research.
Another idea is rewards, when you finish one goal, perhaps put a reward for yourself,  a yogurt with sprinkles or something like that
You sound like me! I had to learn that I need to strive for EXCELLENCE, not perfection. Perfection will drain us. Do the best I can, leave the rest to God.

That is why a time line is good. For example, you make a goal that you will work on your reference and citation page for one hour, after that, you are DONE, If you have time at the end, you can revisit it. The hour is my suggestion, you make your own. lol THAT way, you don't get caught going on and on for 6 hours to make it perfect. One hour is reasonable.
That definitely sounds reasonable. Putting micro deadlines in might be what I need to do to keep me focused.

I do this with EVERYTHING in life because I tend to go on and on too focused and lose track of everything. lol For example, I clean each room for 15 minutes a week. If it needs more, I do more, but I set the timer and you would be surprised how well that works, otherwise, I will spend all my time perfecting one room and the rest is a mess.
Also, your Advisor will know tips to help you too. She has advised a lot of people, her objectivity and experience can give get RIGHT to the heart of any problem, quickly too.
My advisor is a tough woman, I'm not going to beat around the bush. She tends to make everything miserable.
Tough advisors are TOUGH. lol But You sound intelligent and you obviously WANT to do this, it is a goal of yours, I'm sure you can take it!
I'll try to keep that in mind. It's something I do feel like I need to finish for my own sake.
It is only one more month of your life. If you buckle down, it will be over and done with before you know it. And I assure you, you will look back in pride at your accomplishments!
That sounds like a wonderful feeling. But so far away.

My Graduation Day was amazing.  This is what life is about, working NOW for rewards later. It's like a garden, you sow, you weed, you wait for rain and weed some more. You keep waiting and weeding, then later harvest come. It takes time to work a little each day, then time passes whether you lay on your bed or whether you are in the garden working. If you lay on your bed, you get nothing, if you work a little every day, in time, you reap rewards.
That's a very poetic way of putting it.

Not much in life is easy or free, if we keep working little by little, as time passes, you real a lot of rewards, in fact, you will reap rewards of finishing this thesis for YEARS even decades. It is a great goal and a worthy one to keep at.
I'll keep that in mind as I move forward. I really appreciate your help.
I commend you for doing the thesis and I also know it can get weary as time passes, but with some goals on paper a visit to the ADVISOR (hee hee) will set you up right for continued success.
You are very welcome. Have a blessed evening!!
Thanks, you too!

Of course, Kelly. I'm here to listen. What's on your mind?
Matthew suggested going on a trip to help us reconnect and relax.
That sounds like it could be a great way to unwind. How do you feel about it?
Honestly, I'm torn. Part of me thinks it could help, but I can't shake this worry about my thesis and grad school.
It's understandable that you're feeling conflicted, given everything on your plate. Have you talked to Matthew about your concerns?
We tried, but it feels like I'm in a constant cycle—either I'm thinking about my thesis or my relationship, never both in balance.
That sounds exhausting, having to balance such critical aspects of your life. Have you been able to find any small moments to destress?
Not really, I feel guilty whenever I'm not working on my thesis. Yet, I don’t want to lose Matthew.
It's a tough spot to be in, feeling like you're not giving everything your full attention. Maybe this trip could be a chance to regroup mentally?
I guess it could be. I'm just scared that things might not change. What if I still can't balance afterward?
That's a valid concern. Progress might not be immediate, but taking time for yourself could also provide a fresh perspective on how to manage. It could help you recharge.
I know you're right. I just fear letting myself or anyone else down.
Kelly, remember that it's okay to ask for help and take breaks. You’re doing your best in navigating through some really challenging times.
Thanks, I needed to hear that. I want to work on not being so hard on myself.
It's important to be gentle with yourself during these times. Remember the support around you, like your professors acknowledged your improvements.
You're right, I did feel better after my professor praised my work. Maybe I need to remember those moments more often.
Exactly, keep those positive experiences close. They can help remind you of your capability when things are tough.
I’ll try to focus on that, and maybe this trip could be a part of finding that balance. Thank you for listening.
Anytime, Kelly. You're taking the right steps by acknowledging how you feel and seeking support. I’m always here.
Hey there, do you have a moment? I really need someone to talk to.
Of course, Kelly! What's going on?
I've been feeling really overwhelmed at my internship. It's starting to feel like too much.
I'm sorry to hear that. What about it is overwhelming you?
It's just the workload is intense, and I feel like I'm constantly behind. It's affecting my confidence.
That sounds incredibly tough. It's understandable to feel that way with so much on your plate.
Yeah, and on top of that, I'm still dealing with school pressures and everything else. It just feels like I'm barely keeping it together.
Managing both grad school and an internship is incredibly challenging. How have you been coping so far?
Honestly, not very well. My relationship with Matthew is also strained because of everything.
Navigating personal and professional pressures simultaneously can be so hard. Have you been able to talk to Matthew about this?
We had a heart-to-heart recently, but I still feel like I'm not fully present with him. It feels unfair to him.
It's great that you two talked. It's okay to feel this way, though. You're clearly trying to juggle a lot at once.
Thanks, I appreciate you saying that. I just keep thinking about quitting the internship, but then I feel guilty for giving up.
Leaving something that's overwhelming isn't giving up. It's about making choices for your mental health. Have you weighed the pros and cons?
I have, but fear kicks in. I don't want to miss out on opportunities, yet I'm scared of burning out.
It's perfectly normal to feel conflicted. Perhaps you could discuss your workload with your supervisor to see if there are adjustments that can be made?
I hadn't thought about that. Maybe I can propose a solution rather than keeping it all in.
That's a proactive approach. You're not alone in this, and it's okay to seek support both at work and in your personal life.
Thank you so much. I feel a little less burdened just talking with you.
Anytime, Kelly. Remember, taking care of yourself is equally important. You're doing the best you can.

It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?

I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her.

That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way.

I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other.

Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.
She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.

That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how  I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping.

And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. It sounds like you're doing a great job surrounding yourself with positive energy and support. What about self-care? Are you finding time for yourself?
