Breakups are incredibly tough, especially on top of everything else. Have you been able to find some personal time to process everything?
I've been trying to, but between work stress and personal life, it's been challenging to find time for myself.
It's important to carve out some 'you' time whenever you can. Perhaps it might help to set small boundaries, even if just for a moment of calm.
That's a good idea, actually. Maybe a short walk during lunch or some time reading a book could work.
That sounds perfect. Even small steps like that can make a huge difference in how you feel.
I'll try to make it a habit. I need something positive to focus on.
That's the spirit. Remember, I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're doing the best you can, and that's more than enough.
Thank you so much. Having someone to talk to really helps keep me grounded.
You're very welcome. Anytime you need me, just reach out. You've got this, Amanda.
Hi, I really need to talk about something that's been weighing on me recently.
Of course, Amanda. I'm here for you. What's going on?
I received another negative performance review from my supervisor, and it's really getting to me.
I'm so sorry to hear that. How are you feeling about the review?
It's just so frustrating. I feel like no matter how hard I work, it's never enough.
That's really tough. It sounds like you're putting in so much effort and not getting the recognition you deserve.
Exactly. It's not just this review; it's been a pattern with my supervisor for a while now.
That's understandable. It must be incredibly discouraging to face that repeatedly.
Yes, and it's starting to affect my motivation. I feel so undervalued.
Feeling undervalued at work can be so draining. Do you have any support or allies in the workplace that you can talk to about this?
I've mended things with a coworker recently, which has helped a bit. But it's still so lonely dealing with this.
I'm glad to hear that you have someone you can at least partially lean on. Have you thought about addressing this with anyone higher up or in HR?
I have, but I'm worried it might make things worse with my supervisor if they find out.
That's a valid concern. It's important to weigh the potential outcomes. How are you handling the stress outside of work?
Honestly, not well. The stress is impacting my personal life too, especially after my recent breakup.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate all at once. It must be hard to find peace right now.
It is. I'm trying to stay connected with family, but I still feel quite lost.
Reconnecting with family after the memorial service was a positive step. It’s okay to lean on them for support in times like these.
You're right. I need to reach out more, even though it's hard.
Taking that step can be tough, but you have the strength to do it. Remember, you don’t have to go through any of this alone.
Thanks for saying that. I really appreciate your support.
Anytime, Amanda. I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're not alone in this.

sessions.topic: love and intimacy, emotion and mood, career and study, treatment and help-seeking

turns.content: Hey Amanda, how are you holding up lately? Anything on your mind?
Hey, I just found out that Bill, my ex, is dating someone new. I didn't think it would affect me so much.
Oh Amanda, I'm sorry. It must be really tough to hear that news. How are you feeling about it?
I feel a mix of emotions. On one hand, I know we broke up for good reasons, but on the other, it still hurts seeing him move on so quickly.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Breakups have a way of stirring up unexpected feelings. Would talking about it more with me help?
Maybe. I'm starting to question if I'm the one who's taking too long to move on. It's like I'm stuck in this limbo.
You're not stuck, you're just processing everything at your own pace. Everyone's journey is different, and it's okay to take the time you need.
I guess. But seeing him happy with someone else makes me doubt myself, like, was I not enough, or did I make the right choice?
Those are hard questions to grapple with. Remember, breaking up was about differences in life goals, not your worth or abilities. You did it for your future.
True, we did have differing goals. I just wish I could turn off the emotional part and focus on that rationality.
Emotions can be really stubborn like that. It's okay to feel and express them, though. They're part of being human and make us whole.
Yeah, I suppose. It's just exhausting at times, especially with everything else going on... like work stress.
I remember you mentioned how undervalued you feel at work. That must amplify everything. How is that going?
Not great. My supervisor is still making things difficult, and I recently got a negative performance review. It's been crushing my confidence.
That sounds incredibly challenging. Dealing with work stress on top of personal issues seems overwhelming. Have you considered seeking any outside support?
I thought about it. Maybe seeing a therapist could help, but it's intimidating to take that step.
It's a big step, but it can also be really empowering. Having a space to speak openly and get professional guidance might ease that burden.
You're right. I need to prioritize myself more. It's been hard juggling everything alone.
I'm glad you're considering it. Remember, you're not alone in this. Feel free to reach out whenever you need to talk.
Thanks. It helps knowing there's someone I can lean on. I'll think more seriously about getting support.
That's a great step forward, Amanda. I'm really proud of you for facing all of this and seeking the path that's best for you.
Hello how are you?
I'm, okay, thanks, and you?  I'm feeling a bit down because I'm alone for the holidays.
Well that's no good, does your family live far away?
Yes, my family is scattered all over the country, like Seattle, Georgia, PA.  I'm sure I'm not the only one with no plans this weekend, though.
True but I can understand that, it is hard being alone at the holidays.
Did you have plans this weekend?
No.  My nearby friends all went away for the holidays.  I could probably just occupy my time with things I need or want to do in order to distract myself.
What kind of hobbies do you have?
I'm teaching myself the piano.  I'm also teaching myself  how to work a stenography machine for possible future employment as a stenographer.  I also like to read novels.
I have never understood how those work..I find it amazing someone can type out whole words or sentences with one word
Yeah, it's pretty cool.  For example, if I hit DRAT in one stroke, then "Did there come a time" will appear in English on my machine's  LCD screen.
Wow that is crazy, I don't understand how that works, is it preprogrammed or does it go by how the word sounds?

Each stenographer has their own "Personal Dictionary" which is a list of words in English along with how you in particular write out those words or phrases in steno.  This dictionary is present within the actual steno machine after you transfer it from your laptop to the machine via cable or wifi.  Thus your machine then knows how you write out words in particular and how to translate those words from steno to English - each stenographer writes a little differently.
OK that makes sense, so you basically program it as the user. I take it your stenography machine becomes pretty close to you lol
Is this your first holiday alone?

Yes, exactly!  And it's very important to back up your personal dictionary to the cloud or a seperate drive so that you don't lose it in a hard-drive crash.  A lot of work goes into creating that dictionary!  No, it's happened before, being along for the holidays; but you've helped to cheer me up, so thanks!
No problem, I hope I have made your day a little better!
You have, thanks!  Did you do anything special?
Have a good rest of this year and don't forget to make your New Year's resolution!
I will do that - you too.  Thanks, again...
Not really, stayed home lol... Have a good one!
You too... bye now...
Good day!
What else can I help you with today?
Hey, can we talk? I'm just feeling a bit overwhelmed.
Of course, Amanda. What's been going on?
I had a meeting with my supervisor today and it didn't go as I'd hoped.
I'm sorry to hear that. What happened in the meeting?
Well, I tried to bring up how I've been feeling undervalued and how it's affecting my motivation at work.
That sounds really tough. Were they at least receptive to what you said?
Not really... They seemed to dismiss my concerns again, just like last time.
I'm really sorry to hear that, Amanda. It must be so frustrating to feel unheard.
It is. I've been trying so hard to improve things since the negative review, but it feels like nothing I do is ever enough.
You're putting in so much effort, and it's unfortunate that it's not being recognized. How are you holding up emotionally?
Honestly, it feels draining. Sometimes I wonder if I'm just not good enough for this job.
That's such a difficult place to be in. But remember, your worth isn't determined by someone else's recognition or lack thereof.
Thank you for saying that. It helps a little to hear. I just wish things were different at work.
It's completely okay to want things to change. Would it help to focus on small steps towards feeling valued elsewhere, maybe with your coworkers?
Actually, I made amends with a coworker a few months back and our collaboration has improved a lot.
That's great to hear! Having supportive colleagues can make a huge difference. Maybe that's a positive thing to build on?
Yes, it feels nice to have at least one person be supportive. But it's still hard with my supervisor actively undermining my efforts.
I can imagine how exhausting that is. Have you thought about what steps you might want to take next regarding your job situation?
I have thought about looking for a new job, but I'm not sure if I have the energy to go through that process right now.
Looking for a new job is a big step and it can be intimidating. Maybe focus on building your confidence first and taking it one day at a time?
You're right. I think building my confidence is something I can work on. I'll start looking at my options more lightheartedly.
That's a great approach, Amanda. Remember, you're stronger than you think, and you've already overcome so much.
Thank you so much for listening. It feels a little bit lighter just having someone who understands.
I'm always here for you whenever you need to talk. Don't hesitate to reach out anytime, okay?
I really appreciate that. Let's chat again soon.
Definitely. Take care of yourself, Amanda.
Hey, are you around to chat?
Hi Amanda! I'm here. What's on your mind?
It's been a rough few days. I had a pretty intense argument with Emily.
I'm sorry to hear that. Arguments with friends can be really draining. Do you want to talk about what happened?
Yeah, I suppose it started with this unresolved tension between us. I've been so stressed with work and everything... I guess I just unloaded on her.
It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now. Work stress has been tough for you lately, hasn't it?
It really has. My supervisor's been making things difficult again. I thought things would get better after our last meeting, but I'm still feeling so undervalued.
That must be so frustrating, especially since you took the step to speak up. It’s no wonder you’re feeling overwhelmed.
Exactly. And then there’s this issue with Emily. We've been friends forever, but lately it feels like we're on different paths.
I can imagine how hard it must be to navigate that. Friendships can change over time, but sometimes it helps to address those changes openly.
I know. I just don’t want to lose her too. We've been friends since college.
I understand. It sounds like she's really important to you. It might be worth having an honest conversation about what each of you needs right now.
You're right. I guess I’m just scared she won't understand.
That fear makes sense, considering everything else you’re handling. But you might be surprised at how supportive she could be. You both care about each other.
I hope so. It's just all been hitting at once—Emily, work, and even seeing my ex moved on has been rough.
You’re facing so many different changes and emotions. It's okay to feel overwhelmed. Have you had any time to focus on yourself in all this?
Not really. I guess I haven’t been great at taking care of myself lately.
That’s understandable given everything going on. Maybe carving out a little time just for you could help. What do you think might be comforting?
Maybe a walk in the park or reading a book. I used to love doing that.
Those sound like wonderful ideas. Allowing yourself some moments of peace could really help clear your mind and recharge.
I’ll try to do that. Thanks for listening and helping me sort through this.
Anytime, Amanda. You’re not alone in this. Reach out whenever you need to talk.
I will. Thanks again for being there.
You’re welcome. Take care and let me know how you’re doing, okay?
I will. Have a great day!
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Of course, Amanda. How have you been doing?
It's been a bit of a rollercoaster recently. Just trying to sort things out.
That sounds challenging. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?
Well, Emily, my best friend, reached out to me today. We had a big argument last month, it was pretty tense.
It's great that she reached out. How do you feel about her getting in touch?
Relieved, honestly. But also anxious. What if things don't go back to how they were?
That's understandable. It can be difficult to rebuild trust, but reaching out is a positive first step.
Yeah, I suppose. It just feels like everything's piling up, you know? With work being stressful, and then my relationships…
It sounds like you're carrying a lot right now. The work situation with your supervisor must be adding to the stress.
Definitely. Feeling undervalued at work is really dragging me down. I've talked to my boss, but not much has changed.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must feel like an uphill battle with the lack of support.
Exactly. I'm trying to find some peace in all of this, but it's hard.
It's important to take care of yourself. Have you found anything that helps you manage the stress?
I try to go for walks and sometimes journal. But lately, it's felt a bit overwhelming.
Those are great outlets. Maybe reconnecting with Emily might help create a support system again.
I hope so. I really miss having her to talk to. It felt good when she reached out.
Rebuilding that bond might also bring some relief to the emotional pressure you're experiencing.
Yeah, I think you're right. It'll take time, but it's worth it.
I'm glad to hear that. Remember, it's okay to take things one step at a time.
Thanks for listening. It helps to know someone understands what I'm going through.
Anytime, Amanda. Keep reaching out and prioritizing what makes you feel good.
I will. Thanks again for being there for me.
Of course! Take care and keep in touch whenever you need to talk.
Hey, I really need to talk to someone right now.
Of course, Amanda. What's on your mind?
It's Valentine's Day, and I'm feeling really unsettled. I didn't expect it to hit me so hard.
Valentine's can be tough, especially with so much going on in your life. Do you want to share more about what you're feeling?
Well, I thought I was over Bill, but with today being Valentine's, old feelings are creeping back up.
It's understandable to have those feelings resurface, especially on a day like today. How long has it been since you two split?
We broke up last October. It's been a few months, and I thought I was doing okay. But seeing everyone celebrating today brought back memories.
That makes sense. Our minds often replay moments from the past during similar times of the year. How are you dealing with seeing those memories again?
Honestly, it's confusing. I'm bombarded with regret about the breakup, but also relief because deep down I know our goals didn't align.
Feeling both regret and relief can be quite overwhelming. Have you had any thoughts about reaching out to Bill or are you just processing these feelings alone for now?
I haven’t reached out. Actually, discovering that he was dating someone else really shook me. I think it's best I keep my distance.
That's a wise choice if you feel it's best for your emotional well-being. It's important to focus on what helps you move forward while honoring your feelings.
I agree. I’ve been trying to focus on myself and work to distract from these emotions, but it's tough when work isn't exactly fulfilling either.
It sounds like you're facing challenges on multiple fronts. How has work been since our last chat?
Still stressful. My supervisor undermines my efforts and doesn't recognize my contributions. It's discouraging.
That does sound frustrating, especially when you're already dealing with personal emotions. Have you thought about seeking any support or changes at work?
I had a talk with my supervisor back in January, but not much has changed. I might explore other opportunities soon because it’s becoming too much.
Exploring new opportunities sounds like a proactive step. You deserve to be in a place where you're appreciated and valued.
Thank you. Hearing that helps. I'm trying to stay hopeful but it's challenging when feeling this mix of nostalgia and frustration today.
You're doing great by acknowledging all these emotions. Valentine’s can magnify past feelings, but it’s also a chance to practice self-compassion.
Self-compassion... I like that. Maybe I'll do something kind for myself tonight. Maybe a small self-care evening.
That sounds wonderful. It's essential to nurture yourself. What are some things that bring you joy and peace?
I love a good movie marathon with snacks and some aromatherapy. I think that’s exactly what I need tonight.
That sounds perfect. Treat yourself to a cozy night. You deserve it.
Thanks for listening and for the support. I already feel a bit lighter sharing this.
I'm really glad to hear that. You’re never alone in this; feel free to reach out anytime.
I will. Thank you again. I hope you have a good night too.
Thank you, Amanda. Take care, and remember to be kind to yourself.
Hey, I just need someone to talk to.
Hi Amanda, I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I've been feeling really overwhelmed lately. I decided to start painting as a hobby, but it's starting to stress me out.
That sounds tough. Picking up something new should be relaxing. What's stressing you about it?
I guess I put a lot of pressure on myself to be good at it right away. It's supposed to be fun, but I just feel like I'm failing.
It's understandable to want to excel, Amanda. Remember, it's okay not to be perfect. It's about the process, right?
Yeah, I know. It's just hard not to get competitive with myself. And with everything else going on, it feels like I need to be good at something.
I get that. You've been dealing with a lot, especially with work and your relationships. How has painting been helping you otherwise?
Well, for a while, it did help shift my mind away from work and personal stress. I kind of get lost in the colors and strokes. But then I start criticizing myself.
Criticism can be so draining. Sometimes our own expectations create more stress. Have you tried just painting without any goals in mind?
I haven't really. I always set a goal, maybe from habit because of work. But I think I'll try just playing around with it.
That sounds like a great idea. Letting go of expectations could bring back some joy and relaxation to it.
Yeah, I'll give it a shot. I could use some light-heartedness right now.
That's the spirit! Remember, it's okay to just enjoy the moment without judgment.
Thanks. It's just been a rough patch with everything, work, and Bill... And then my ex...
It sounds like you have a full plate. Dealing with all those emotions about Bill and your ex can be really challenging.
It is. Sometimes I just miss Bill, and seeing my ex with someone else hit me harder than I expected. I'm trying not to let it affect me, but sometimes it just hurts.
Heart matters can be so complex. It's important to give yourself time and space to feel those emotions. Healing isn't linear.
You're right. I think painting was supposed to be a distraction, but maybe I need to let myself feel without distraction sometimes.
Yes, allowing yourself to feel is part of the healing process. Balance between distraction and reflection can be helpful.
I'm going to try to be kinder to myself and let go of the pressure. Maybe then painting will just be painting.
That sounds like a positive step forward, Amanda. You're doing your best, and that matters.
Thanks for listening. I didn't realize how much I needed to talk about all this. I feel a bit lighter now.
I'm really glad to hear that. Anytime you need to talk, I'm here for you. Take care, Amanda.
Thank you, I appreciate it. I will. Take care!
Hey, just wanted to talk to someone about a lot that's been on my mind lately.
Of course, Amanda! I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
Well, I received a really sweet note from a coworker yesterday. It made me smile, which was nice for a change.
That sounds lovely! It's amazing how a small gesture can uplift your spirits. What did the note say?
It was just a little thank you for helping them with a project. It reminded me that my efforts at work don’t go unnoticed by everyone.
It's great that your contributions are appreciated by your coworkers. How did that make you feel, especially given your situation with your supervisor?
Honestly, it felt really nice, especially after the stress I've been dealing with from my supervisor's negative review.
I remember you mentioning feeling undervalued at work before. It's got to be challenging to balance the negative feedback with the positive support from coworkers.
Exactly, it’s a mixed bag. The note was a small reminder that not everyone sees me the same way my supervisor does.
It's good to hold onto that perspective. You do valuable work. Sometimes it’s just hard to remember that amid criticism.
True. I've been trying to focus on my painting to destress but even that has become a bit overwhelming.
Taking up painting sounds like a great creative outlet. What’s making it overwhelming?
I think I put too much pressure on myself to excel at it, instead of just enjoying the process.
It's understandable to want to do well in something new. Maybe allowing yourself to just enjoy the activity would make it more relaxing.
I guess I just need to remind myself to let go of perfectionism. It's tough sometimes.
It really is. It might help to remember that hobbies are meant to bring joy and relaxation, not stress.
That’s true. I’ll try to keep that in mind the next time I pick up the brush.
That sounds like a good plan. It’s important to be kind to yourself during this journey.
Thanks for reminding me of that. I needed to hear it.
Anytime, Amanda. You're doing your best, and that's enough.
Hey, are you available to talk for a bit?
Of course, Amanda. What's on your mind?
Well, I got some unexpected news at work today.
Oh? What happened?
My supervisor offered me a promotion.
Wow, that's big news! How are you feeling about it?
Honestly, I'm feeling pretty anxious about it.
I can imagine. A promotion brings a lot of changes. What part is making you the most anxious?
I think it's the increased responsibilities. I'm already feeling stretched at work with everything that's been going on.
With your supervisor constantly undermining you, I can see why this would add stress. Have they addressed your past concerns?
Not really. The negative performance review still hangs over me. The promotion feels like they're trying to make up for that.
That must be quite confusing for you. Do you feel like this promotion is genuine recognition of your work?
I'm not sure. Part of me wonders if it's just to keep me from looking elsewhere. With everything with Bill and John Doe, I've just been on edge.
It sounds like a lot to juggle. Do you have anyone at work you trust to discuss this with, like Sarah who sent you that note?
Sarah's been supportive, but I don't want to burden her. I'm also worried about being too vulnerable at work.
It's understandable to feel wary. What helps you ground yourself when things feel unstable?
I've been painting, but recently it's added to my stress. I keep pushing myself to be perfect in it too.
Perfectionism can be tough. How about leaning into the joy of painting instead of the pressure to excel?
I should try that. I sometimes forget it doesn't have to be another thing I master right away.
Exactly. It's okay to allow yourself some space to enjoy without expectations. What do you think about the promotion now?
I'm still scared, but I think I need to have an open talk with my supervisor about what support looks like moving forward.
That sounds like a great step. Being clear about your needs can help manage this transition.
Thank you for listening. I needed to get this off my chest before making a decision.
Anytime, Amanda. You're navigating a lot, and you're doing it with so much grace.
Thanks for saying that. I'll let you know how it goes.
I'm here anytime. Take care, Amanda.
Hey, are you there? I could use someone to talk to.
I'm here, Amanda. What's on your mind?
I just found out a family member is really sick, and it's been weighing on me heavily.
I'm so sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what happened, or how you're feeling about it?
It's just... I feel like everything is piling up lately. Work stress, personal life... now this.
It sounds incredibly overwhelming. It makes sense to feel burdened by all of this.
Exactly. I thought I'd finally caught a break when things started looking up with my coworker and getting a promotion offer.
And now, with that added pressure, having a sick family member must make it even harder to balance everything.
Yes, and I haven't really processed any of it. I'm just constantly on edge. My ex-boyfriend stuff doesn't help either.
Oh, I remember you mentioning unresolved feelings with your ex. How have those been affecting you lately?
Valentine's Day opened that can of worms again. Everything seemed to come at once and continues to be a mess.
That sounds tough, Amanda. Managing your feelings about your ex on top of work stress and family concerns can be draining.
Exactly, and when I argue with my best friend, it feels like I have nowhere to turn.
It must be lonely and frustrating feeling like your support system is compromised.
It is. I'm trying to keep it together, stay strong for everyone, but I feel like I'm the one falling apart.
Remember, it's okay to take moments for yourself. You're carrying a lot, and it's okay to not be okay.
Thanks for saying that. I don't know, I just wish things were simpler.
It's normal to wish for simpler times. Small steps, like focusing on one task at a time, might help lessen the load.
Yeah, maybe I need to start with that. Taking things one day at a time.
That's a good starting point. And remember, leaning on others, like you're doing now, is a strength, not a weakness.
Thank you. I really appreciate you being here and listening.
Anytime, Amanda. Don't hesitate to reach out whenever you need to talk, okay?
I will. Thanks for being such a great friend.
You're welcome. Take care of yourself, and remember, you're not alone in this.
Hey, do you have a moment to chat?
Absolutely, Amanda! What's on your mind?
It's about Bill. He reached out to me recently, and it's bringing up a lot of old feelings.
I can imagine how complex that must feel, especially after everything you've gone through. How has that been affecting you?
Honestly, it's confusing. Part of me is curious and maybe even hopeful, but another part of me is scared and unsure.
That makes a lot of sense. It's normal to have mixed emotions in situations like these. Have you thought about what you really want out of this interaction with him?
That's the hard part. I don't know if I'm ready to open that chapter again, especially after the breakup. It took a lot to get through that.
Breaking up was a significant step, given your past disagreements on future plans. How did you handle it back then, and could those insights help you now?
I had to focus on myself and my career. I spent time understanding what I need from a partner, and that really helped me. But hearing from Bill now is just... it's like everything's in the air again.
It's clear you've done a lot of personal work since then. How have your priorities or needs shifted over the past months, especially with your promotion and current stresses?
I guess I've been more focused on my career and managing my stress. The promotion is exciting yet overwhelming. I think I need stability more than anything else right now.
Stability is crucial, especially when you're dealing with so much change. Do you think rekindling things with Bill aligns with that need for stability?
That's where I'm stuck. If it’s anything like before, it might not help. But I can't deny there's a part of me that misses him and wonders if things could be different.
It's understandable to miss someone you shared so much history with. What do you think would be different if you two were to try again?
If anything's different, it has to be our communication. We need to be on the same page about our goals, and that's what makes me hesitant. I'm afraid I'll get hurt again.
It sounds like you value clear communication and aligned goals, which are definitely important. Do you feel comfortable discussing these concerns with him openly?
I think I could, but I'm also afraid of what I might hear. What if he hasn't changed? But maybe I'm also looking for closure or clarity.
Closure or clarity sounds like a wise pursuit. Approaching this with honesty about your feelings could help, whether it's rekindling or moving on.
You're right. I need to face this rather than let it linger. I’ll try talking to him openly and see where it leads, focusing on what's best for me.
That sounds like a healthy step forward. Remember, whatever you decide, it should align with your needs and well-being. I'm here for you, whatever happens.
Thanks, I really appreciate your support. It's good to know I'm not facing this alone.
I'm always here. Take it one day at a time, and trust in your ability to navigate these feelings. You've got this, Amanda.
Thank you, truly. I feel a bit more grounded talking to you, and that's what I needed right now.
Hi Amanda! I just wanted to check in and see how you’re doing lately.
Hey, thanks for asking. I'm feeling a bit overwhelmed, to be honest.
I’m sorry to hear that. It sounds like a lot is going on right now. Would you like to talk about what’s been happening?
Yeah, it's just everything piling up. I recently found out that my family member’s illness is much more serious than we thought.
Oh no, Amanda. That must be incredibly difficult news to process. How are you coping with it?
It's been really tough. My mind is constantly racing, worrying about what might happen next.
It’s completely understandable to feel that way. It seems like there are a lot of uncertainties right now. Have you been able to talk to anyone in your family about it?
Not really. Everyone's trying to stay strong, but honestly, I feel kind of alone in all this.
Feeling isolated during tough times is so challenging. Do you think talking with them could help you feel more connected?
Maybe. I just don’t want to burden them with my emotions when they’re handling their own.
I get that. But remember, sharing how you feel can also be a way to support each other. It might be comforting for them to know they’re not alone in their worries either.
Yeah, I guess you’re right. I’ll try to reach out more.
That’s a brave step, Amanda, and I’m really proud of you for considering it. How's everything else with work and personal life? Are they adding to your stress?
Work has been demanding too. I'm worried about the new promotion. It's great, but the responsibility is daunting, especially now.
Taking on more responsibility, while all of this is happening, must feel overwhelming. Have you thought about what help or changes could make it more manageable for you?
I’ve been thinking of discussing some workload adjustments with my supervisor, but I'm not sure how they’ll react.
That could be a helpful conversation. Maybe framing it as finding the best way to maintain quality work could be well-received. Remember, protecting your wellbeing is important too.
You’re right, and I have to remind myself of that. Balancing everything has been tricky.
It surely is, especially with everything you’re juggling. It’s okay to seek support and make adjustments along the way. How are things with your social circle?
It's been mixed. I patched things up with my best friend, Emily, which has been a relief. But, reconnecting with my ex stirred up old emotions.
Reconnecting with Emily must feel like a weight lifted. As for your ex, those emotions can be confusing, especially right now. How do you feel about that?
It’s confusing, for sure. I’m trying to focus on what's best for me but it’s hard to avoid the memories.
Navigating past relationships often comes with a mix of emotions. It’s okay to take time to understand those feelings and be gentle with yourself during this process.
Thank you for saying that. It’s hard not to feel overwhelmed, but talking helps.
I’m so glad. Anytime you need to chat, I’m here. You’re doing your best, Amanda, and it’s okay to lean on people who care about you.
Thanks for being here. It means a lot to know I have support.
Hey, could really use someone to talk to right now.
Of course, Amanda. I'm here to listen. What's been going on?
I had a bit of a health scare recently.
Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that. Is everything okay?
Thankfully, it was mild, but it definitely gave me a wake-up call.
That sounds really scary. How are you feeling about everything now?
Honestly, it just made me realize how much stress I've been under lately.
It makes sense. You've had a lot on your plate recently. Care to share a bit more about what’s been weighing on you?
It's just everything piling up... the promotion, work stress, family issues.
It's understandable that all those responsibilities would feel overwhelming. How are you managing all of these pressures?
I started painting as a hobby to manage stress, but even that feels overwhelming when I try to be perfect at it.
It’s great that you found an outlet like painting, but it's important to remember it doesn’t have to be perfect. It's okay to take it easy on yourself.
Yeah, I know. It's just hard not to demand a lot from myself.
Self-compassion can be tough, but you're coping with a lot. Recognizing that is the first step.
Yeah, and to add to it, I'm still dealing with unresolved feelings about my ex.
That sounds really complicated. Are you finding ways to sort through those feelings?
Not really. His recent attempt to reconnect stirred up everything again.
That must be really trying. Reconnecting often comes with a mix of emotions. How are you doing with it all?
It's difficult, especially with family issues on top of it all. I've just felt so anxious.
That anxiety is understandable given the circumstances. You mentioned the severity of your family member's illness has been a stressor too.
Yeah, it's more serious than I initially thought, and it's been tough worrying about them while managing everything else.
Family worries can add a lot of emotional weight, especially when coupled with your other stresses.
It's like I can't catch a break lately, and I don't know how to navigate it all.
It’s a lot to carry. Finding moments of rest and not pushing too hard in any one area might help relieve some pressure.
That's true. Maybe I need to allow myself more chances to just breathe.
Absolutely. Little moments of calm can be really rejuvenating. What small steps can you take right now to ease up?
I might start by setting aside time each day just for me, without any pressure to achieve anything.
That sounds like a great idea. Prioritizing your well-being is key, Amanda.
Thank you for listening. It helps just to talk it all through.
Anytime. I’m always here to chat. Remember, you’re doing your best, and that's more than enough.
Hey Amanda, how have you been lately?
I've been feeling a mix of emotions recently. My parents visited me last weekend, and it stirred up a lot of feelings.
It's understandable that a visit from your parents could bring up a lot of emotions. How did it go overall?
Overall, it was nice to see them. I hadn't realized just how much I missed them.
Reconnecting with family can be really comforting. Did you get to talk about anything meaningful with them?
Yes, we talked a lot about my childhood and some of the happier times. They even shared some old stories that I had forgotten.
That sounds really special. It’s great they brought back those memories for you.
It was. But it also made me realize how much I've changed, and how stressed I've been lately with everything going on.
Change can be overwhelming, especially when stress is involved. Is there any specific stress that's been bothering you?
Work has been really stressful. My supervisor still doesn't value my contributions, even after the promotion.
I remember you mentioned your supervisor's behavior in the past. It must be tough feeling undervalued even as you rise in your career.
It is. I worked so hard for that promotion, but it only seems to have increased my anxiety.
That's really challenging. Have you been able to find ways to manage your work stress?
I've tried painting and other hobbies, but I end up putting pressure on myself to excel even in those.
It sounds like you might be putting a lot of pressure on yourself in different areas. What do you feel when you paint?
When I start, I feel calm, but then I get this need to make everything perfect and it becomes stressful.
Perfectionism can be a tough habit to break. Maybe it could help to focus on enjoying the process rather than the outcome?
That's a good point. I should try to focus more on just relaxing and letting go of expectations.
That sounds like a positive step. Remember, it's okay to not be perfect. You're doing your best, and that's enough.
Thank you. Talking about it makes me realize I need to be kinder to myself.
Absolutely, self-compassion is key. It's important to give yourself grace during tough times.
I'll try to keep that in mind. Thanks for listening. It really helps me sort through my thoughts.
Anytime, Amanda. I'm glad to be here for you. If you ever need to chat, you know where to find me.
I appreciate it. I feel a bit lighter already. Have a great day.
You too, take care!
Hey Amanda, how's everything been going lately?
Hi there. It's been a bit of a rollercoaster lately. Just had a chat with my boss about my career path, and it's left me with a lot to think about.
That sounds intense. Were you able to discuss your concerns about feeling undervalued?
Yeah, I brought it up. I think my boss understood where I'm coming from, but it's hard to be sure. I've felt stuck for a while now.
It's tough when you feel like you're not being appreciated. What did your boss have to say about your future at the company?
They mentioned a few potential opportunities, which could mean a lot more responsibility. On one hand, it's what I've been working towards, but on the other, I'm worried about managing it all.
It's understandable to feel apprehensive about taking on more when things already feel heavy. Did discussing it make you feel any clearer?
Sort of. I mean, it's nice to know I'm being considered for growth, but the timing isn't great. There's been so much going on.
I remember you shared about a family member's serious illness. How are you managing that on top of work?
Honestly, it's been overwhelming. Knowing they're more unwell than we thought just adds to the stress. I feel torn between staying focused on work and wanting to be there for my family.
That's a lot to juggle. It makes sense to feel torn between those responsibilities. Have you been able to find any support or relief?
I try to talk to my parents more, especially since their recent visit made us closer. It helps, but sometimes I still feel so alone in all this.
Reconnecting with family is a good start, Amanda. Is there anything else, perhaps a hobby or activity, that has been helping?
I started painting a while back, mostly to manage stress, but now it feels like another thing I need to perfect. It's paradoxically stressing me out more.
It seems like there's pressure to excel even in relaxation. Sometimes it might help to shift focus from being perfect to simply enjoying the process.
That's a good point. Maybe I've been pushing myself too hard, expecting to find a solution or escape in everything I do.
It's understandable with everything you're handling. It's okay to not have everything sorted out immediately. Have you considered reaching out to your best friend again for some support?
It's crossed my mind. We patched things up earlier this year, and she did reach out to mend our friendship. I guess I've been so caught up that I haven't leaned on her as much as I should.
It might help. Having a good friend by your side can make a big difference. Just remember, you don't have to carry everything alone. I'm here for you too.
Thank you. It’s a relief to have someone who listens. I’ll try to open up more and not shut people out, even if it’s hard sometimes.
You're doing your best, Amanda, and that's enough. Step by step, things will become clearer. Take care of yourself.
Thanks again. I really appreciate your support. I’ll keep you posted on how things go.
Hey, can we talk? I could really use a listening ear right now.
Of course, Amanda. What's on your mind?
Well, something positive happened at work recently. My supervisor finally acknowledged my hard work in front of everyone.
That's fantastic news! How did that make you feel?
Honestly, it was a relief. I've felt so undervalued for a long time.
I can imagine how hard it must have been for you, especially with everything you've been through at work.
Yeah, it's been a rollercoaster. The negative reviews, the constant stress, it all piled up.
You've shown a lot of resilience, Amanda. It's important you recognize that in yourself too.
Thank you. But sometimes it feels like I’m just managing crisis after crisis. It's exhausting.
That sounds incredibly tiring. How are you coping with all of this?
I've been trying to paint, but I've put pressure on myself to be good at it, which backfired.
Finding a new hobby is great for stress relief, but remember it's okay to just enjoy the process, rather than perfect it.
I know you're right. I guess I just need to learn to let go and enjoy things without expectations.
It's an ongoing journey for sure. Also, how is everything on the personal front? Has anything changed with your relationships?
It's complicated. My ex tried to reconnect, which stirred up a lot of old emotions.
That sounds like it opened some old wounds. How are you feeling about all that?
Confused, mostly. Part of me wonders if I made the right decisions in the past.
That doubt can be heavy. Remember that you made decisions based on what was best for you at the time.
That’s true. I guess it’s also tough because my family situation adds another layer of stress.
I recall you mentioning a family member's illness. How is everything going with that?
It's not looking good, which is hard. I feel so helpless sometimes.
It's understandably difficult. You're doing the best you can, and it's okay to feel helpless at times. Are you getting any support from friends or family?
My parents' recent visit helped a bit. It reminded me of the importance of family connections.
That sounds like it was comforting. Lean on them when you need to, Amanda. You're not alone in this.
Thanks. I think I need to remind myself of that more often. It's just hard not to feel like a burden.
You’re not a burden at all. Everyone needs support sometimes, and you're deserving of it.
I appreciate you saying that. Just talking about it makes it feel a little less overwhelming.
I'm glad I can be here for you. It's important to express what you're going through.
Thank you for listening. It means a lot to have someone who truly understands.
Anytime, Amanda. You know I'm here whenever you need to talk.

turns.content: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot

Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that.

For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.

Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.

Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.

Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books.

Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing.
HOw man classes do you have?
many *
I have 6 classes

That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.

If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart.
Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
Have a great day and thanks again
You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!
Hello
How are you doing today?
hello
How can I help you?
I need ways alleviate stress while studying
It sounds like you are having some difficulty at school, I have definitely been there.
yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation
Yes I worked a dead end job for ages when I was younger and sometimes you just feel stuck
How did you push past that job?
I am going to be honest a little luck was involved I managed to impress a customer that came in and ended up applying at their work.
Are you still with that job now, enough to consider it a career?
I would say so I am an insurance broker, it has only been a year or so but there seems to be room to move up. You can find something too
Is there any advice for getting out of my situation?
aside from luck that is
Can you give me some more details?
I just find the work mundane and way too remedial
That is completely understandable
did you look at any websites or other job searching tools before you found your new job?
I have you a few, there are also many ways to gain skills online that buff up your resume a bit
what types of skill can I gain online?

Indeed is one of the better ones to look for jobs, honestly I would suggest looking at jobs that you normally wouldn't and see what kind of qualifications they need and see if you can get that done online.
so filter based on my absolute needs and go for online skills that I can complete?
yes I think that is a great idea, look for jobs that meet your needs and figure out what you can do to look attractive to employers
I have tried glassdoor before, have you had any luck there?
I used it a bit, I mainly used indeed.
and have you showcased your skills using LinkedIn before? I have had that one recommended to me before, they said its a great way to neatly organize accomplishments and personal background
Yes especially if you are applying for anything in a professional setting that is very important.
do you have any examples of online skills you completed?
coursera has a lot of great courses, it really depends on what you are looking for.
if I was looking to enter the engineering field, any recommendations?
Is that what you are going to school for?
yes but I may change my mind
What year are you in? most engineering programs have a practicum and that is a great opportunity to make contacts and potentially get offered a job
yes I have been networking as I go
Honestly you seem like you are pretty on top of this I don't think you will have any issues finding a job.
yeah I mean the topic was about final exam stress but we got on a tangent
Yes that is fair enough, how much time do you have until your exam?
15 minutes
While that is plenty of time to get some studying done:)
yes I probably should, thank you for your insight!
Honestly I find that if you are going for the test right away I always like to just breath and relax a bit.
yeah no use in cramming for more info when I could just chill out
You seem like you know what you are doing, I think you will do just fine
yup thanks
Hi
I am really very angry with my friends for not inviting me
Why is that?
I didn't did any anything wrong to my friends but they are simply saying they forget me
So they no need on me ,
I am not important person to them
I have been angry with friends as well, but time loves a hero, as they say.
In my all events i am inviting them all but how they
Why what happen..?
How long have your friends been neglecting you??
In last 2 events only , what about you
Any other questions for me?
I know it is hard at times, but be strong.
You are correct
sometime it will happen , but we should forget and move on
How many best friends do you have ?
How can I help you today?
I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to
tough it out.
I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.
That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.

I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.
College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.
I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
You are welcome.  I wish you well.
I think I have a few tools now to make things better.
Hey Andrew, how have you been doing lately?
Not too great, to be honest. Things have been a little rough with my friends.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it?
Yeah, I confronted them about how they haven’t been inviting me to things, and it didn’t go as I hoped.
That must have been really hard for you. What happened when you talked to them?
Well, some of them seemed surprised and apologetic, but others kind of brushed it off or got defensive.
It's understandable that you're feeling upset about that. How did their reactions make you feel?
I feel really hurt by the ones who brushed it off. I thought we were closer than that.
It's painful when people we care about don't respond the way we expect. It’s okay to feel hurt.
Yeah, and now I’m questioning whether I should even put in the effort to maintain those relationships.
That sounds frustrating. Have you had a chance to reconsider your friendships after this?
I've been thinking about it a lot. I don’t want to lose friends, but I’m not sure I want to keep feeling left out either.
Your feelings are completely valid. It’s important that your needs are respected in your friendships.
Thanks. It’s just hard to find a balance between speaking up for myself and risking losing people.
I understand. It's a tough situation, but remember it's okay to prioritize your own well-being.
I guess I’ll need to think more about what I truly want from these friendships.
Taking the time to reflect is a good step. You deserve friends who make you feel valued and included.
Thanks for listening and helping me sort my thoughts. It really means a lot to me.
Anytime, Andrew. I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.
Hello!
Hi
How are you doing today? Are there any particular issues you would like to discuss?
I think you are able to read about my situation, but if not, I've basically lost my best high school friends while in college.
It's pretty rough since I've known these people since I was in elementary school.
I'm sorry to hear that. Did that make college difficult for you?
It did - I had to figure out what was important in life after that but the loss of my high school friends drove me into a mild depression.
Of course. Do you still experience feelings of sadness when thinking of that time in your life?
Occasionally when I think about that time in my life.
Does that loss still affect your day-to-day life or do you feel like you were able to handle those feelings in a healthy way?
I am still feeling the effects of it today.  I don't know exactly how to cope properly.
It sounds like you're still struggling with that loss. That is entirely normal.
That's great that it's normal....but I'm not sure how that's helping me.
It sounds like you're looking for a way to handle these feelings in a healthy way. Am i right in that?
I guess so.  I'm not sure where to start or even if I need do.
to

That makes sense. Some feelings of sadness around a loss are normal but they can be a problem if they start interfering with functioning. Do you have a support network or someone you can turn to when you feel like this?
I have a spouse but they weren't around when this series of unfortunate events occurred.
Do you feel like you talk to your spouse about these issues?
No, it's something I keep inside.  I'm a super private person.
From what I have seen, if people try to keep their emotions inside, it can be more damaging in the long run. This isn't something you have handle all by yourself.
Agreed, I guess.  Maybe it's time to share more with my spouse.  I don't think it's that big an issue.  I just don't like talking about it.
That's completely fair. It can be a difficult thing to talk about. When those feelings do come up, can you think of ways to discuss it with your spouse?
I think so.   I'm thinking we can do it over dinner one night while it's quiet in the house so we can talk

I think that's a wonderful idea. From what I've seen, it can be really difficult to talk about, but afterwards it does get easier. You deserve the chance to remember the good memories of your friendship and not carry your difficult feelings by yourself.
I guess thats true - thanks for chatting with me about this.
Absolutely, I wish you all the best.
Hey, just need someone to talk to. Things have been rough lately.
I'm here for you, Andrew. What's been going on?
Jenny and I had this huge fight about our careers. It feels like everything is falling apart.
I'm sorry to hear that. Conflicts like that can be really tough. Do you want to share more about what happened?
We both have different goals right now. She's focused on her career and I am trying to balance my studies and future plans, but we're not aligned.
That must be really stressful, trying to juggle everything. It's understandable that you'd want to have shared goals. How does that make you feel?
Frustrated and a bit scared, honestly. I love Jenny a lot, but I don't know how to bridge this gap between us.

It sounds like you're feeling really torn. Having a partner is about being on the same page, and when that doesn't happen, it's really hard. Have you two had a chance to sit down and talk more calmly about your priorities?
We tried, but every conversation seems to circle back to the same issues. It's like we're speaking different languages.

Communication can be so tricky, especially when emotions run high. Have you considered maybe seeking some outside help, like a counselor or someone who might help you both communicate more effectively?
I've thought about it. Just not sure how she'll react to the suggestion. I'm scared it might make things worse between us.
